meta.description: 桌游本体 — 统一定义游戏中的静态结构概念与流程时序概念。不定义具体游戏规则。
meta.convention:
每个概念的 constraints.required 表示：若另一个概念继承或引用此概念，则必须提供这些字段的值。程序递归收集父链上的所有 required 约束和顶层字段。

类型约定（type field convention）：字段的 type 值分为三类——(1) 概念引用：type 为已有概念的 id（如 player、zone、object、cost、content、information_visibility），表示该字段的值是对该概念实例的引用。带有 | null 后缀表示可空；(2) 泛引用：type 为 concept_ref，表示引用目标不限于单一概念，程序或 LLM 需根据上下文确定具体目标类型；(3) 原始类型：直接使用类型名——string、integer、boolean、any、map<string, any>、enum。enum 类型附带内联的 enum 数组枚举合法值。

交叉引用约定（cross-reference convention）：所有 definition 和 field description 文本中，引用其他概念时使用 <concept_id> 占位符包裹概念 id。例如「指向游戏中一个具体的 <object> 实例（<player>、<zone>、<piece> 等，均为 <object> 的子类）」。LLM 读取时可据此识别交叉引用并沿 <concept_id> 查找对应概念的定义。

definition.zh: 可被识别、引用或操作的实体或抽象概念。
definition.en: An entity or abstract concept that can be identified, referenced, or operated upon.

description.zh: 描述该对象固有特征的键值对集合。由游戏规则预定义，描述对象「是什么」而非「此刻怎样」。注意：attributes 对应的是 Property（属性），不是 State（状态）。
description.en: A map of key-value pairs describing the object's intrinsic characteristics. Predefined by game rules. Describes what the object 'is', not what it 'currently is' (which would be State).

description.zh: 唯一标识符。所有 <object> 实例必须通过此字段被识别和引用。由 <object> 自身定义，隐式赋予所有子类实例。
description.en: Unique identifier. All <object> instances must be identifiable and referenceable through this field. Defined by <object> itself, implicitly available to all subclass instances.

description.zh: 描述对象固有特征的键值对集合。由游戏规则预定义，描述对象「是什么」而非「此刻怎样」。
description.en: A map of key-value pairs describing the object's intrinsic characteristics. Predefined by game rules. Describes what the object 'is', not what it 'currently is'.

definition.zh: 直接参与游戏并能够做出决策的实体。<player> 是游戏中的能动主体——它发起 <action>、拥有 <object>、积累 Score、最终参与胜负判定。<player> 继承自 <object>。
definition.en: An entity that directly participates in the game and is capable of making decisions. <player> is the active agent in the game — it initiates <action>s, owns <object>s, accumulates Score, and ultimately participates in victory determination. <player> extends <object>.

description.zh: 玩家在回合顺序中的位置（从 1 开始）。用于决定行动先后。若游戏采用其他顺序机制（如同时行动、竞标决定顺序），此字段可为空。
description.en: The player's position in turn order (1-based). Used to determine action sequence. May be empty if the game uses other ordering mechanisms (e.g. simultaneous action, bidding).

description.zh: 玩家名称，用于 UI 显示和 LLM 自然语言生成，不影响规则逻辑。
description.en: Player name for UI display and LLM natural language generation. Does not affect rule logic.

description.zh: 玩家在回合顺序中的位置（从 1 开始）。若游戏采用同时行动等非固定顺序机制可省略。
description.en: Player's position in turn order (1-based). May be omitted for games with non-fixed ordering like simultaneous action.

definition.zh: 一种可被 <player> 拥有、计数、转移和消耗的价值概念。<resource> 继承自 <object>。其核心特征是可计量——玩家持有的是「3 个蓝宝石」而非「一个叫蓝宝石的物件」。同一类型的 <resource> 的所有个体完全等价、可互相替代。与 <marker> 的区别在于：resource 会被 action 的 <cost> 消耗或作为 <effect> 产出，而 marker 只用于指示状态。
definition.en: A value concept that can be owned, counted, transferred, and spent by <player>s. <resource> extends <object>. Its defining feature is countability — a player holds '3 blue gems', not 'a thing called blue gem'. All units of the same <resource> type are completely equivalent and interchangeable. Unlike a <marker>, a resource is consumed by an action's <cost> or produced by an <effect>; a marker only indicates state.

description.zh: 此资源的计量单位。如宝石用「颗」、钱币用「枚」、木材用「根」。仅供 UI 和 LLM 生成自然语言时使用，不影响规则逻辑。
description.en: The unit of measurement for this resource. E.g., '颗' for gems, '枚' for coins. For UI and natural language generation only; does not affect rule logic.

description.zh: 此资源的外观描述。如「蓝色六边形宝石，表面有切割纹理」「金黄色圆形硬币，正面有五角星图案」。用于动画生成、UI 渲染和 AI 讲解时帮助玩家识别实物，不影响规则逻辑。
description.en: Visual description of this resource. E.g., 'blue hexagonal gem with cut texture', 'golden round coin with a star on the front'. Used for animation, UI rendering, and AI explanations to help players identify physical pieces. Does not affect rule logic.

description.zh: 用于表示此资源的那个看得见摸得着的小零件。如棕色八角柱代表食物。若为 null，说明此资源本身外观特征明显、玩家一看就知道是什么（如璀璨宝石的扑克筹码——宝石本身就是那样），不需要额外说明「用哪个零件代表它」。
description.en: The tangible small piece used to represent this resource. E.g., a brown octagonal pillar represents food. If null, the resource itself has obvious visual characteristics and players can identify it at a glance (e.g., Splendor's poker chips — the gem is self-evidently what it is), so no extra explanation of 'which piece represents it' is needed.

description.zh: 资源计量单位（如「颗」「枚」「根」），仅供 UI 和 LLM 自然语言生成使用，不影响规则逻辑。
description.en: Unit of measurement for this resource (e.g., 'piece', 'token', 'stick'). For UI and LLM natural language generation only; does not affect rule logic.

description.zh: 资源外观描述——形状、颜色、图案等关键视觉信息。用于 UI 渲染和 AI 向玩家解释规则时帮助识别实物。
description.en: Visual description of this resource — shape, color, patterns. Used for UI rendering and AI explanations to help players identify physical pieces.

description.zh: 用于表示此资源的物理 <token>。如棕色八角柱代表食物。null 表示资源本身辨识度高，不需要额外的小零件来代表。
description.en: The physical <token> used to represent this resource. E.g., a brown pillar represents food. null means the resource is self-evident and needs no extra piece to represent it.

definition.zh: 一种特殊的 <resource>，代表玩家在游戏中获得的分数或胜利点数（victory points）。<score> 继承自 <resource>，核心特征是可被计数和增减，通常不用于支付费用或转移给其他玩家，而是用于胜负判定。典型例子包括璀璨宝石中的声望点数、文明演化中的分数。
definition.en: A special <resource> representing a player's points or victory points. <score> extends <resource>. Its defining feature is that it is countable and can be increased or decreased; it is typically not spent as a cost or transferred to other players, but is used for victory determination. Typical examples include prestige points in Splendor and score points in Civolution.

definition.zh: 可通过 <play> 进入游戏、并通过自身 <effect> 改变游戏状态的游戏零件。<piece> 继承自 <object>。<piece> 与 <token> 的本质区别：<piece> 携带 <effect>，可以被 <play>——打出它、建造它、激活它，游戏状态会因此改变。<effect> 的静态形态就是 <property>——「这张牌的费用是 3 蓝」「打出后获得 2 分」「每轮结束时获得 1 银币」都是 <effect> 的规格说明。<token> 没有 <effect>，不能被 <play>——<token> 只负责标记某个事实，<token> 本身不做任何事。
definition.en: A game component that enters the game through <play> and changes game state through its own <effect>s. <piece> extends <object>. The essential difference between <piece> and <token>: a <piece> carries <effect>s and can be <play>ed — when you play it, build it, or activate it, the game state changes as a result. <effect>s in static form are <property>s — 'this card costs 3 blue', 'gain 2 points when played', 'gain 1 silver at the end of each round' are all <effect> specifications. A <token> has no <effect>s and cannot be <play>ed — <token>s only mark facts; a <token> itself does nothing.

description.zh: 此物件的外观描述。必须包含 AI 向玩家解释规则时所需的关键视觉信息——信息标注在什么位置、图案和颜色长什么样。如「矩形卡牌，左上角白色数字为该牌的分数，中央下方为效果文本」「棕色六角形厚纸板片，正面中央印有白色城堡图案，无数字标注」。AI 回答「怎么看」类问题时主要依赖此字段。
description.en: Visual description of this piece. Must include key visual information needed for AI to explain rules to players — where information is printed, what patterns and colors look like. E.g., 'rectangular card, the white number in the top-left is the victory points, effect text is centered below', 'brown hexagonal tile with a white castle icon in the center, no numbers'. AI relies on this field when answering 'how do I see...' questions.

description.zh: 物件外观描述，必须包含 AI 向玩家解释规则时所需的关键视觉信息——信息标注位置、图案和颜色。AI 回答「怎么看」类问题时主要依赖此字段。
description.en: Visual description of this piece. Must include key visual information for AI to explain rules — where information is printed, patterns and colors. AI relies on this field for 'how do I see...' questions.

definition.zh: 一种承载游戏状态的物理组件。<board> 继承自 <object>。与 <aid> 的本质区别：<aid> 是纯被动参考物——上面的信息只是画上去的，收起来也不影响游戏；<board> 则承载游戏状态——上面可以放置 <piece> 和 <token>、可以容纳 <zone>（zone 虽由规则定义，但 board 是它的物理宿主）、可以携带自身的 <content>（如玩家面板上印着的活动图标能力，不依赖任何外部 <piece> 即可使用）。与 <piece> 的本质区别：<piece> 可以被 <transfer>——打出、交换、弃掉、移动；<board> 不可被转移——它固定属于某个 <player> 或公共区域，整个游戏过程中不会易主。<board> 的子类包括 <public_board> 和 <player_board>。
definition.en: A physical component that carries game state. <board> extends <object>. The essential difference from <aid>: an <aid> is a purely passive reference — the information on it is merely printed, and putting it away does not affect the game; a <board> carries game state — <piece>s and <token>s are placed on it, it can host <zone>s (zones are defined by rules, but the board is their physical host), and it can carry its own <content> (e.g., the activity icon ability printed on a player console, usable without any external <piece>). The essential difference from <piece>: a <piece> can be <transfer>red — played, exchanged, discarded, moved; a <board> cannot be transferred — it is fixed to a <player> or the public area and never changes hands during the game. Subclasses include <public_board> and <player_board>.

description.zh: 此版图的外观描述。必须说明形状、材质、尺寸和上面印了什么。如「折叠式硬纸板，展开后为 60cm×40cm 的矩形版图，表面印有世界地图、区域边界和计分轨」「约 A4 大小的硬纸板，印有模组槽位、阶段区和各种标记格」。
description.en: Visual description of this board. Must describe shape, material, size, and what is printed on it. E.g., 'folded cardboard board, 60cm×40cm when unfolded, printed with a world map, region borders, and a scoring track', 'roughly A4-sized cardboard printed with module slots, stage partitions, and various marker spaces'.

description.zh: 此版图上承载的 <zone>。key 为 zone 的 id（如 "<income_chip_area>"），value 为对象，至少包含 `position`（该 zone 在版图上的物理位置描述，如「左上角」「右半部」），可选包含 `description`（补充说明）。注意：zone 本身由规则独立定义——board 不「创造」zone，board 只是 zone 的物理宿主。客人问「某某东西放哪」时，系统通过此字段找到位置信息并给出精确回答。
description.en: The <zone>s hosted on this board. Key is the zone id (e.g., "<income_chip_area>"); value is an object containing at minimum `position` (physical location description on the board, e.g., 'top-left corner', 'right half'), optionally `description` for additional notes. Note: zones are independently defined by rules — the board does not 'create' zones, it is merely their physical host. When a guest asks 'where do I put X', the system uses this field to find the position and give a precise answer.

description.zh: 此版图自身携带的效果或能力。不需要打出任何 <piece> 即可使用——这些能力直接印在版图上，由版图自身赋予玩家。例如 Civolution 玩家面板上的基础活动图标。数组中的每项描述一个独立的能力或效果。这些内容在版图进入游戏时自动生效，不依赖任何外部 <piece>。
description.en: Effects or abilities carried by this board itself. Usable without playing any <piece> — these abilities are directly printed on the board and granted to the player by the board itself. E.g., the basic activity icon on a Civolution player console. Each entry in the array describes one independent ability or effect. These contents take effect automatically when the board enters the game, independent of any external <piece>.

description.zh: 版图外观描述——形状、材质、尺寸和上面印有的内容。AI 向玩家介绍版图布局时的核心信息来源。
description.en: Visual description of this board — shape, material, size, and what is printed on it. Core information source when AI introduces board layout to players.

description.zh: 此版图承载的 <zone> 及其物理位置。key 为 zone id，value 含 position 字段。客人问位置相关问题时系统从此字段检索。仅当此 board 上确实有 zone 时才需填写。
description.en: The <zone>s hosted on this board with their physical positions. Key is zone id; value contains a position field. The system searches this field when guests ask position-related questions. Only needed when this board actually hosts zones.

description.zh: 此版图自身携带的效果或能力——不依赖任何外部 <piece> 即可使用。如玩家面板上印着的基础活动图标。
description.en: Effects or abilities carried by this board itself — usable without any external <piece>. E.g., the basic activity icon printed on a player console.

definition.zh: 用于向 <player> 展示参考信息、辅助玩家识别和操作的游戏实体。<aid> 继承自 <object>。其核心特征是「不承载游戏状态」——它上面的信息只是画上去的，不因游戏进程而改变；它上面不放置 <piece> 或 <token>，也不容纳 <zone>。<aid> 是纯参考物：规则书被合上、玩家提示卡被收起来，游戏规则依然存在并生效。熟练玩家在脑中记住了所有规则后，完全可以不借助 <aid> 进行游戏。注意：如果一块板子上面可以放置棋子、需要翻面、会被放标记——它承载游戏状态，则它不是 <aid>，应归入 <board>。
definition.en: A game entity used to present reference information to <player>s and assist in recognition and operation. <aid> extends <object>. Its defining trait is that it 'carries no game state' — the information on it is merely printed and does not change with gameplay; no <piece>s or <token>s are placed on it, and it hosts no <zone>s. An <aid> is a pure reference: close the rulebook, put away the player aid, and the game rules still exist and apply. A skilled player who has memorized all rules can play entirely without <aid>s. Note: if a board has pieces placed on it, needs to be flipped, or receives markers — it carries game state — then it is not an <aid> and should be categorized as a <board>.

description.zh: 此辅助物的外观描述。必须说明形状、材质、尺寸和上面印了什么。如「折叠式硬纸板，展开后为 60cm×40cm 的矩形版图，表面印有世界地图、区域边界和计分轨」「210mm×148mm 的过塑卡片，正面印有所有行动的图标速查表」。
description.en: Visual description of this aid. Must describe shape, material, size, and what is printed on it. E.g., 'folded cardboard board, 60cm×40cm when unfolded, printed with a world map, region borders, and a scoring track', '210mm×148mm laminated card with a quick-reference icon chart of all actions printed on the front'.

description.zh: 此辅助物在视觉上对应哪些 <zone>。注意：Aid 不「包含」这些 zone，它只是把它们画在了上面——这种映射是单向的视觉关联。Zone 的存在和属性完全由规则定义，与 Aid 无关。
description.en: Which <zone>s this Aid visually corresponds to. Note: the Aid does not 'contain' these zones; it merely depicts them. This is a one-way visual association — Zones exist and have properties defined purely by rules, independent of any Aid.

description.zh: 辅助物外观描述——形状、材质、尺寸和上面印有的内容。AI 向玩家介绍版图布局和辅助工具时的核心信息来源。
description.en: Visual description of this aid — shape, material, size, and what is printed on it. Core information source when AI introduces board layout and helper tools to players.

description.zh: 视觉映射——声明此 Aid 在视觉上对应哪些 <zone>。只有确实对应某个/某些 zone 的 Aid（如版图、轨道）才需要填写；规则书、玩家提示卡等纯文档型 Aid 可省略。注意：Aid 不「包含」这些 zone，它只是画出了它们。Zone 的存在和属性完全由规则定义，与 Aid 无关。
description.en: Visual mapping — declares which <zone>s this Aid visually corresponds to. Only fill this when the aid actually depicts zones (e.g. boards, tracks); document-type aids such as rulebooks and player aids may omit it. Note: the Aid does not 'contain' these zones; it merely depicts them. Zones exist and are defined purely by rules, independent of any Aid.

definition.zh: 桌游中最常见的小型物理零件。<token> 继承自 <object>。它代表盒子里那些看得见摸得着、但自身高度抽象的小零件——八角柱、圆片、方块、米宝等。一个 <token> 本身不决定自己代表什么；它与游戏概念的关联是外在的、可变的——同一个棕色八角柱，放在仓库里代表食物，放到重置轨上代表重置标记。<token> 本身不携带 <effect>，不能被 <play>——它不会因为被放置或移动而自己改变游戏状态；真正改变状态的是规则 <event>。例如把伤害 <token> 放到卡上，卡「受伤」这个 <state> 才生效；消耗 1 个食物对应的 <token> 的是某个 action 的 cost，而不是 <token> 自己。
definition.en: The most common small physical piece in board games. <token> extends <object>. It represents those tangible, highly abstract little parts in the box — octagonal pillars, discs, cubes, meeples, etc. A <token> itself does not determine what it represents; its association with game concepts is external and mutable — the same brown pillar represents food when in the storage area, and a reset marker when placed on the reset track. A <token> itself carries no <effect> and cannot be <play>ed — placing or moving it does not change game state by itself; the rules <event> does. For example, placing a damage <token> on a card makes the 'wounded' <state> take effect; spending the <token> representing food is the cost of an action, not an effect of the token.

description.zh: 此指示物的外观描述。如「直径 15mm 的圆形塑料圆片，蓝色半透明」「15mm×15mm 的方形木质方块，红色」「10mm 直径的球形玻璃珠，金色」。
description.en: Visual description of this token. E.g., '15mm diameter round plastic disc, blue translucent', '15mm×15mm square wooden cube, red', '10mm diameter spherical glass bead, golden'.

description.zh: 此指示物代表什么逻辑概念。如伤害 Token 指向 State「受伤」、起始玩家 Token 指向 State「起始玩家」。若一个 Token 是多用途的（红色方块既能计分又能标归属），此字段为空，Token 的具体含义由它当前所在的 Zone 或使用上下文决定。
description.en: What logical concept this token represents. E.g., a damage token points to State 'wounded', a starting player token points to State 'starting_player'. For multi-purpose Tokens (a red cube that can track score or mark ownership), leave this empty — the Token's meaning is determined by its current Zone or usage context.

description.zh: 指示物外观描述——形状、尺寸、颜色、材质。Token 的外观是 AI 向玩家解释实物识别时的核心信息。
description.en: Visual description of this token — shape, size, color, material. Appearance is the core information for AI to help players identify physical pieces.

description.zh: 此 Token 代表什么逻辑概念（如 State「受伤」、State「起始玩家」）。若为多用途 Token（如红色方块既计分又标归属），则省略此字段，含义由所在 Zone 或上下文决定。
description.en: What logical concept this Token represents (e.g., State 'wounded', State 'starting player'). Omit for multi-purpose Tokens — meaning is determined by Zone or context.

definition.zh: 用于指示某个 <state> 或位置的概念。<marker> 继承自 <object>。它不被当作资源消耗，而是被放置、移动或移除来反映游戏规则中的状态变化。典型例子包括：阶段标记、天气标记、进程轨标记、计分标记、起始玩家标记等。
definition.en: A concept used to indicate a <state> or position. <marker> extends <object>. It is not spent as a resource; instead it is placed, moved, or removed to reflect state changes defined by the rules. Typical examples include phase indicators, weather indicators, progress track markers, score markers, and starting player markers.

description.zh: 此标记物的外观描述——形状、尺寸、颜色、材质。如「直径 15mm 的圆形塑料圆片，蓝色半透明」「六边形厚纸板片，正面印有太阳图标」。
description.en: Visual description of this marker — shape, size, color, material. E.g., '15mm diameter round plastic disc, blue translucent', 'hexagonal cardboard piece with a sun icon printed on the front'.

description.zh: 用于表示此标记物的那个看得见摸得着的小零件。如蓝色圆片代表分轨标记。若为 null，说明此标记物本身外观特征明显、玩家一看就知道是什么（如璀璨宝石的起始玩家标记——两个零件拼成钻石形状，不需要额外解释）。
description.en: The tangible small piece used to represent this marker. E.g., a blue disc represents a score track marker. If null, the marker itself has obvious visual characteristics and players can identify it at a glance (e.g., Splendor's starting player marker — two pieces forming a diamond shape, no extra explanation needed).

description.zh: 标记物外观描述——形状、尺寸、颜色、材质。
description.en: Visual description of this marker — shape, size, color, material.

description.zh: 此标记物代表的逻辑概念（如 State「起始玩家」、State「当前阶段」）。
description.en: The logical concept this marker represents (e.g., State 'starting player', State 'current phase').

description.zh: 用于表示此标记物的物理 <token>。如蓝色圆片代表分轨标记。null 表示标记物本身辨识度高，不需要额外的小零件来代表。
description.en: The physical <token> used to represent this marker. E.g., a blue disc represents a score track marker. null means the marker is self-evident and needs no extra piece to represent it.

definition.zh: 用于标记谁是起始 <player> 的 <marker>。<starting_player_marker> 继承自 <marker>。它是许多桌游中的通用组件——持有此标记的 <player> 即为当前 <round> 的起始玩家。每 <round> 结束后，标记传递给下一位 <player>，对应的 <starting_player> 状态随之更新。
definition.en: A <marker> used to mark who is the starting <player>. <starting_player_marker> extends <marker>. It is a common component in many board games — the <player> holding this marker is the starting player for the current <round>. After each <round>, the marker is passed to the next <player>, and the corresponding <starting_player> state is updated.

description.zh: 起始玩家标记的外观描述。形状、材质和大小因游戏而异——如「由两个零件拼成的钻石形状」（璀璨宝石）、「一枚金色皇冠状纸板指示物」（卡坦岛）、「一只大型木质米宝」（卡卡颂）。
description.en: Visual description of the first player marker. Shape, material, and size vary by game — e.g., 'two pieces that fit together to form a diamond shape' (Splendor), 'a golden crown-shaped cardboard token' (Catan), 'a large wooden meeple' (Carcassonne).

description.zh: 此 <marker> 代表的逻辑概念：<starting_player>。持有此标记的 <player> 即为起始玩家。
description.en: The logical concept this <marker> represents: <starting_player>. The <player> holding this marker is the starting player.

definition.zh: 游戏中的抽象逻辑容器，表示一组 <object> 的空间归属关系。不依赖版图和实体，只由规则决定。<zone> 是抽象概念，子类包括 <reserve>、<discard_pile>、<player_zone>、<track> 等。
definition.en: An abstract logical container in the game, representing the spatial belonging of a set of <object>s. Independent of board and physical components; defined solely by rules. <zone> is an abstract concept; subclasses include <reserve>, <discard_pile>, <player_zone>, <track>, etc.

description.zh: 声明此 <zone> 允许存放哪些类型的 <object>。值为本体概念 id 数组（如 ["card", "token"]）。空数组 [] 表示不限制类型。程序校验 <transfer> 时：若 what 的类型不在 contains 中，<transfer> 非法。
description.en: Declares what types of Object this zone allows. Array of concept ids (e.g. ["card", "token"]). Empty array [] means any type is allowed. Programs check this when validating a Transfer.

description.zh: 可容纳的对象数量上限。null = 无上限。达到上限后，以此区域为目标的 Transfer 将被拒绝。
description.en: Maximum number of objects this zone can hold. null = unlimited. When full, Transfers targeting this zone are rejected.

description.zh: Zone 的唯一标识符。继承自 <object>，用于在游戏规则中精确引用特定 Zone 实例。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Zone. Inherited from <object>, used to precisely reference a specific Zone instance in game rules.

description.zh: 声明此 Zone 允许存放哪些类型的 <object>。程序校验 <transfer> 时以此过滤——若 what 的类型不在 contains 中，<transfer> 非法。空数组表示不限类型。
description.en: Declares what types of <object> this Zone allows. Programs check this when validating a <transfer> — if what's type is not in contains, the <transfer> is illegal. Empty array means any type is allowed.

description.zh: 此 Zone 的所有权归属。决定该 Zone 及其中的 <object> 属于哪个 <player>。null 表示公共区域，所有玩家均可访问。
description.en: Ownership of this Zone. Determines which <player> owns this Zone and its contents. null means public — all players can access.

description.zh: 此 Zone 的信息可见性级别。决定 Zone 中的内容可被哪些 <player> 观察——公开区全员可见，手牌区仅拥有者可见，牌堆区仅顶部部分可见等。
description.en: Information visibility level of this Zone. Determines which <player>s can observe its contents — public zones are visible to all, hand zones are owner-only, deck zones may be partially visible at the top, etc.

description.zh: Zone 可容纳的对象数量上限。null 表示无上限。达到上限后，以此 Zone 为目标的 <transfer> 将被拒绝。
description.en: Maximum number of objects this Zone can hold. null = unlimited. When full, <transfer>s targeting this Zone are rejected.

definition.zh: 某个时刻游戏世界中为真的断言。描述游戏实体「此刻怎样」，而非「是什么」。<state> 是运行时事实，随时可被 <effect> 改变。
definition.en: A true assertion about the game world at a given moment. Describes what a game entity 'currently is', not what it 'is'. <state> is a runtime fact, changeable at any time by <effect>s.

description.zh: 此状态描述的实体。回答「谁此刻怎样」中的「谁」。指向游戏中一个具体的 <object> 实例（<player>、<zone>、<piece> 等，均为 <object> 的子类）。例如「Player A 持有 3 个蓝宝石」中，subject = Player A。
description.en: The entity this state describes — the 'who' in 'who is currently in what state'. Points to a concrete <object> instance (<player>, <zone>, <piece>, etc. — all subclasses of <object>). E.g., in 'Player A has 3 blue gems', subject = Player A.

description.zh: 状态值的类型约束。如 "integer"、"boolean"、"player"。程序修改状态时以此校验。
description.en: Type constraint for the state value. E.g., "integer", "boolean", "player". Programs validate state changes against this.

description.zh: 游戏开始时的初始值。用于 setup 和 reset。
description.en: Initial value when the game starts. Used for setup and reset.

description.zh: State 的唯一标识符。用于在规则中精确引用特定状态实例（如「Player A 的分数」「Card X 的横置状态」）。
description.en: Unique identifier of the State. Used to precisely reference a specific state instance in rules.

description.zh: 此 State 描述的实体——回答「谁此刻怎样」中的「谁」。指向一个具体的 <object> 实例（<player>、<zone>、<piece> 等）。
description.en: The entity this State describes — the 'who' in 'who is currently in what state'. Points to a concrete <object> instance.

description.zh: State 值的类型约束（如 integer、boolean、player）。程序修改 State 时以此校验值的合法性。
description.en: Type constraint for the State value. Programs validate state changes against this.

description.zh: 游戏开始时的初始值，用于 setup 和 reset。确保每次游戏开始时 State 从一致的状态出发。
description.en: Initial value when the game starts. Used for setup and reset to ensure consistent starting state.

definition.zh: <object> 或 <zone> 固有的、由游戏规则预先定义的特征。描述游戏实体「是什么」「拥有什么能力」「具备什么特点」。默认不可变——在 <object> 进入游戏时即确定，仅在 <effect> 明确修改时才变化。<property> 是 <cost>、<content>、<effect>、<information_visibility> 的父概念。
definition.en: An intrinsic characteristic of an <object> or <zone>, pre-defined by game rules. Describes what a game entity 'is', 'what abilities it has', 'what traits it possesses'. Immutable by default — set when the <object> enters the game, only changed by an explicit <effect>. <property> is the parent of <cost>, <content>, <effect>, <information_visibility>.

description.zh: 此属性附着于什么概念或实体。回答「谁拥有这个特征」。可以指向本体概念（"card"，表示所有卡牌）或具体实例（"level_1_card_03"）。
description.en: What concept or entity this property attaches to. Answers 'who has this characteristic'. Can point to an ontology concept ("card") or a specific instance ("level_1_card_03").

description.zh: 属性值的类型约束。如 "integer"、"boolean"、"cost_map"、"effect_spec"。
description.en: Type constraint for the property value. E.g., "integer", "boolean", "cost_map", "effect_spec".

description.zh: 是否可被游戏效果修改。默认 false（静态）。若为 true，修改必须经由 Effect 触发，不可被玩家随意更改。
description.en: Whether this property can be modified by game effects. Default false (static). If true, modification must go through an Effect — players cannot arbitrarily change it.

description.zh: 对象被创建或进入游戏时的默认值。
description.en: Default value when the object is created or enters the game.

description.zh: Property 的唯一标识符。用于在规则中精确引用特定属性（如「Card X 的费用」「Zone Y 的可见性」）。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Property. Used to precisely reference a specific property in rules.

description.zh: 此 Property 附着于什么概念或实体——回答「谁拥有这个特征」。可指向本体概念（如 "card"，表示所有卡牌）或具体实例。
description.en: What concept or entity this Property attaches to — answers 'who has this characteristic'. Can point to an ontology concept or a specific instance.

description.zh: Property 值的类型约束（如 integer、boolean、cost_map、effect_spec）。
description.en: Type constraint for the Property value.

description.zh: 是否可被 <effect> 修改。默认 false（静态属性）。若为 true，修改必须经由 <effect> 触发，不可被玩家随意更改。
description.en: Whether this Property can be modified by <effect>s. Default false. Changes must go through an <effect>.

description.zh: 对象被创建或进入游戏时的默认值。确保 Property 始终有定义良好的初始态。
description.en: Default value when the object is created or enters the game. Ensures Property always has a well-defined initial state.

definition.zh: 表示某个 <zone> 或 <object> 归属于哪个 <player> 的 <state>。<ownership> 继承自 <state>。所有权的建立有三种途径：(1) <zone> 推导——<object> 位于 owner 非 null 的 <zone> 中时，该 <zone> 的 owner 隐式拥有该 <object>；(2) 固有归属——<object> 在游戏开始时就已确定属于某 <player>（如玩家自带的牌组），不随 <zone> 变化而改变；(3) 游戏中获取——经由 <transfer>（ownership_change=true）或 <effect> 显式变更所有权。所有权可在游戏过程中被改变——转移、抢夺、赠予或剥夺均须经由规则定义的 <effect> 或 <transfer> 触发。
definition.en: A <state> representing which <player> a <zone> or <object> belongs to. <ownership> extends <state>. It is established in three ways: (1) <zone> derivation — when an <object> is in a <zone> whose owner is non-null, that <zone>'s owner implicitly owns the <object>; (2) Intrinsic — the <object> belonged to a <player> from the start of the game, independent of <zone> changes; (3) Acquired — explicitly changed via <transfer> (ownership_change=true) or an <effect> during gameplay. Ownership can change during the game — transferring, stealing, gifting, or revoking must all be triggered by rules-defined <effect>s or <transfer>s.

description.zh: 拥有所有权的 <player>。<state> 的 subject 字段则指向被拥有的 <zone> 或 <object>。null 表示无所有者（公共区域）。
description.en: The <player> who holds ownership. The <state>'s subject field points to the <zone> or <object> being owned.

description.zh: 所有权的来源。intrinsic = 游戏开始时即确定（如自备牌组）；zone = 由所在 Zone 的 owner 推导（默认行为）；transfer = 经由 Transfer 或 Effect 在游戏中获得。若未指定，程序默认按 zone 推导。
description.en: The source of ownership. intrinsic = determined at game start (e.g., personal deck); zone = derived from containing Zone's owner (default); transfer = acquired via Transfer or Effect during gameplay. If unspecified, defaults to zone derivation.

description.zh: 拥有所有权的 <player>。State 的 subject 字段则指向被拥有的 <zone> 或 <object>。null 表示无所有者（公共区域）。
description.en: The <player> who holds ownership. The State's subject field points to the <zone> or <object> being owned. null = public.

description.zh: 所有权来源：intrinsic（游戏开始即确定，如自备牌组）、zone（由所在 Zone 的 owner 推导，默认行为）、transfer（经由 <transfer> 或 <effect> 在游戏中获得）。若未指定，程序默认按 zone 推导。
description.en: Source of ownership: intrinsic (from game start), zone (derived from containing Zone, default), transfer (acquired via <transfer> or <effect> during gameplay). Defaults to zone derivation if unspecified.

definition.zh: 标记当前<round>或游戏开始时谁最先行动的<state>。<starting_player>继承自<state>。在多数游戏中，起始玩家由物理的<starting_player_marker>标记——持有<starting_player_marker>的<player>即为起始玩家。每<round>结束后，<starting_player_marker>按规则传递给下一位<player>，<starting_player>随之更新。
definition.en: A <state> that marks which <player> acts first in the current <round> or at the start of the game. <starting_player> extends <state>. In most games, the starting player is indicated by a physical <starting_player_marker> — the <player> holding the <starting_player_marker> is the starting player. After each <round>, the <starting_player_marker> is passed to the next <player> according to the rules, and <starting_player> is updated accordingly.

description.zh: 被标记为起始玩家的<player>。从<state>继承——回答「谁此刻是起始玩家」中的「谁」。
description.en: The <player> marked as the starting player. Inherited from <state> — the 'who' in 'who is currently the starting player'.

description.zh: 固定为 boolean。true = 此<player>是起始玩家。
description.en: Fixed to boolean. true = this <player> is the starting player.

description.zh: 游戏开始时为 false——起始玩家在 setup 阶段通过规则确定（如随机抽取或持有<starting_player_marker>）。
description.en: Initially false — the starting player is determined during setup (e.g., randomly or by holding the <starting_player_marker>).

definition.zh: 游戏过程中发生的、被游戏规则所识别和定义的、对游戏 <state> 或流程有意义的、不可再分的原子事实。<event> 是流程本体的根概念——一切「发生了什么」都始于 <event>。子类包括 <transfer>、<action>、<trigger>、<resolve>、<activation>、<play>。
definition.en: An atomic fact that occurs during gameplay, recognized and defined by game rules, meaningful to game <state> or flow, and not further divisible. <event> is the root of the procedure ontology — everything that 'happens' starts from <event>. Subclasses include <transfer>, <action>, <trigger>, <resolve>, <activation>, <play>.

description.zh: 导致此事件发生的主体。若事件由玩家主动发起（如 <action>），actor 为该 <player>。若事件由规则自动引发（如 Trigger），actor 为 null。
description.en: The entity that caused this event. If initiated by a player (e.g. <action>), actor is that <player>. If automatically triggered by rules (e.g. Trigger), actor is null.

description.zh: 此事件作用的目标。可以是任意 <object> 的子类实例（<player>、<zone>、<piece> 等）。若事件无特定目标（如「回合开始」），target 为 null。
description.en: The target this event acts upon. Can be any <object> subclass instance (<player>, <zone>, <piece>, etc.). If the event has no specific target (e.g. 'turn begins'), target is null.

description.zh: 此事件发生前必须满足的 <condition> 列表。用于在事件执行前进行合法性校验——若任一 <condition> 不满足，事件不可发生。空数组或省略表示无条件。
description.en: A list of <condition>s that must be met before this event can occur. Used for legality validation before execution — if any <condition> is unmet, the event cannot occur. Empty array or omission means unconditional.

description.zh: 此事件的执行规则说明。以中英双语描述事件执行时的具体约束——如「所选宝石颜色必须两两不同」「若不足 3 色则取走全部可用颜色」。这些规则描述超出了结构化字段的表达能力，供 LLM 理解规则和程序实现参考。
description.en: Execution rules for this event. Bilingual description of specific constraints during execution — e.g., 'chosen gems must be of distinct colors', 'if fewer than 3 colors available, take all available'. These rules describe constraints beyond what structured fields capture, serving as reference for LLM understanding and program implementation.

description.zh: Event 的唯一标识符。用于在规则中精确引用特定事件实例，追溯游戏历史中的因果关系链。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Event. Used to precisely reference a specific event instance and trace causal chains in game history.

description.zh: 导致此 Event 发生的主体。<action> 中必为 <player>，<trigger> 中为 null。若 Event 由规则自动引发则省略。
description.en: The entity that caused this Event. Required for <action>s (always a <player>), null for <trigger>s. Omitted if the Event is automatically triggered by rules.

description.zh: 此 Event 作用的目标——可以是任意 <object> 的子类实例。若 Event 无特定目标（如「回合开始」）则为 null。
description.en: The target this Event acts upon. Can be any <object> subclass instance. null if the Event has no specific target.

description.zh: 此 Event 发生前必须满足的 <condition> 列表。空数组或省略表示无条件触发。
description.en: A list of <condition>s that must be met before this Event occurs. Empty or omitted means unconditional.

description.zh: 此 Event 的执行规则说明（中英双语）。描述结构化字段之外的具体约束，供 LLM 和程序实现参考。
description.en: Execution rules for this Event (bilingual). Describes specific constraints beyond structured fields, for LLM and program reference.

definition.zh: 用于判断某个命题在当前游戏 <state> 下是否成立的表达式。<condition> 本身不改变任何东西——它只回答「是」或「否」。<condition> 是 Rule Engine 的核心判断单元：<action> 的合法性检查、<trigger> 的激活判断、<endgame_condition> 的触发检测，全部由 <condition> 驱动。
definition.en: An expression that evaluates whether a proposition is true under the current game <state>. A <condition> changes nothing — it only answers 'yes' or 'no'. <condition> is the core judgment unit of the Rule Engine: <action> legality checks, <trigger> activation, and <endgame_condition> detection are all driven by <condition>s.

description.zh: 此条件的参数。内容由具体的条件类型决定。例如 SupplyCount 条件：{ "resource": "blue", "operator": ">=", "value": 4 }。复合条件（AND/OR）：{ "op": "and", "operands": [condition_ref, ...] }。程序根据条件的 id 查找对应的 evaluator 函数，传入 params 和当前 GameState，返回 boolean。
description.en: Parameters for this condition. Content is determined by the specific condition type. E.g., a SupplyCount condition: { "resource": "blue", "operator": ">=", "value": 4 }. Compound conditions (AND/OR): { "op": "and", "operands": [condition_ref, ...] }. The program looks up the evaluator function by the condition's id, passes params and current GameState, and returns a boolean.

description.zh: Condition 的唯一标识符。程序根据此 id 查找对应的 evaluator 函数，传入 params 和当前 GameState，返回 boolean。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Condition. The program looks up the corresponding evaluator function by this id, passes params and current GameState, and returns a boolean.

description.zh: 此 Condition 的参数，内容由具体的条件类型决定（如 SupplyCount 条件：{ resource, operator, value }）。程序根据条件 id 查找 evaluator 并传入 params。
description.en: Parameters for this Condition. Content is determined by the specific condition type. The program looks up the evaluator by condition id and passes these params.

definition.zh: 时间轴上的一个位置。<timing> 回答「何时发生」，是游戏时间秩序的基础。<timing> 可以是：某个状态变化的瞬间（「任何使宝石总数变化的 <event> 结算完成时」）、阶段边界（「一名 <player> 的回合结束时」）、或某个 <event> 完成后（「此 <action> 执行完毕时」）。<timing> 的持有者有两类：一是 <trigger>——决定何时检查 <condition>，时机到达且条件满足才触发；二是 <procedure>（<round>、<turn>、<phase>）——划定自身的起止边界。普通 <event> 不持有 <timing>——<trigger> 触发后其 <event> 序列按 order 依次执行，顺序本身就是时序，无需逐事件声明。<timing> 本身不改变游戏状态，它只是时间秩序的描述。
definition.en: A position on the timeline. <timing> answers 'when does it happen' and is the foundation of the game's temporal order. A <timing> can be: the instant of a state change ('when any <event> that changes the gem total finishes resolving'), a phase boundary ('when a <player>'s turn ends'), or the completion of some <event> ('when this <action> finishes executing'). <timing> has two kinds of holders: <trigger>s — which use it to decide when to check the <condition>, firing only when the timing arrives and the condition holds; and <procedure>s (<round>, <turn>, <phase>) — which use it to delimit their own start and end. Ordinary <event>s do not hold <timing> — once a <trigger> fires, its <event> sequence executes in order, and the sequence itself is the temporality; no per-event declaration is needed. <timing> itself changes no game state — it is merely a description of temporal order.

description.zh: 此时机的参数，内容由具体的时机类型决定。例如事件完成后：{ "after": "<event_id>" }；阶段边界：{ "boundary": "turn_end" }；状态变化瞬间：{ "on_change": { "zone": "<zone_id>", "watch": "count" } }。程序根据时机的 id 查找对应的 watcher 函数，在游戏循环中侦测时机是否到达，返回 boolean。
description.en: Parameters for this timing. Content is determined by the specific timing type. E.g., after an event completes: { "after": "<event_id>" }; a phase boundary: { "boundary": "turn_end" }; the instant of a state change: { "on_change": { "zone": "<zone_id>", "watch": "count" } }. The program looks up the watcher function by the timing's id, detects in the game loop whether the timing has arrived, and returns a boolean.

description.zh: Timing 的唯一标识符。程序根据此 id 查找对应的 watcher 函数，在游戏循环中侦测时机是否到达。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Timing. The program looks up the corresponding watcher function by this id and detects in the game loop whether the timing has arrived.

description.zh: 此 Timing 的参数，内容由具体的时机类型决定（如阶段边界：{ boundary: "turn_end" }）。程序根据时机 id 查找 watcher 并传入 params。
description.en: Parameters for this Timing. Content is determined by the specific timing type (e.g., phase boundary: { boundary: "turn_end" }). The program looks up the watcher by timing id and passes these params.

definition.zh: <effect> 的内部组成部分之一——指明一个 <effect> 在被触发前必须被履行的代价。<cost> 继承自 <property>。其形态不限于支付 <resource>：支付 3 个蓝宝石是 <cost>，横置一张牌是 <cost>，弃掉一张手牌是 <cost>，跳过下个回合也是 <cost>。<cost> 的运行时逻辑：(1) 由 <condition> 检查前提是否可满足；(2) 满足后执行对应 <event>（<transfer>、状态变更等）。<cost> 不满足则该 <effect> 不可触发。<cost> 可以为空（免费效果），但此时 <content> 不可为空。
definition.en: An internal component of an <effect> — specifies the cost that must be fulfilled before the <effect> can be triggered. <cost> extends <property>. Its form is not limited to <resource> payment: paying 3 blue gems is a <cost>, tapping a card is a <cost>, discarding a card is a <cost>, skipping a turn is a <cost>. Runtime logic: (1) a <condition> checks if the prerequisite can be met; (2) if met, the corresponding <event> executes (<transfer>, state change, etc.). If the <cost> is not satisfied, the <effect> cannot be triggered. <cost> may be empty (free effect), but <content> must not be empty in that case.

description.zh: 此费用的参数。内容由具体的 Cost 类型决定——不限于资源支付。典型结构：支付资源 { "resources": { "blue": 3 } }、弃牌 { "discard": 1 }、牺牲 { "sacrifice": "piece_ref" }、横置 { "tap": "self" }、跳过回合 { "skip": "next_turn" }。程序根据 params 的内容构造对应的 Condition（检查前提是否可满足）和 Event（执行实际动作）。复合费用（AND/OR）通过 params 内部结构表达。
description.en: Parameters for this cost. Content is determined by the specific cost type — not limited to resource payment. Typical structures: pay resources { "resources": { "blue": 3 } }, discard { "discard": 1 }, sacrifice { "sacrifice": "piece_ref" }, tap { "tap": "self" }, skip turn { "skip": "next_turn" }. Based on params, the program constructs a corresponding Condition (to check if the prerequisite can be met) and Event (to execute the actual action). Compound costs (AND/OR) are expressed through the internal structure of params.

description.zh: 此 Cost 的具体参数——不限于资源支付。如支付资源 { resources: { blue: 3 } }、弃牌 { discard: 1 }、横置 { tap: "self" }。程序根据 params 构造对应的 Condition（检查前提）和 Event（执行动作）。
description.en: Specific parameters for this Cost — not limited to resource payment. E.g., pay resources, discard, tap. The program constructs corresponding Conditions and Events based on params.

definition.zh: <effect> 的内部组成部分之一——描述 <effect> 结算时应当发生的具体事件。<content> 继承自 <property>。由一个或多个待执行的事件描述组成（如造成伤害、抽取卡牌、获取 <resource>、移动 <token>、改变 <state>、摧毁 <piece> 等），在 <resolve> 阶段被实例化为真实的 <event> 并应用到游戏状态。<content> 与 <cost> 互补构成完整的 <effect>：<cost> 先执行，<content> 后发生。<content> 可以为空，但 <cost> 和 <content> 不可同时为空。
definition.en: An internal component of an <effect> — describes the specific events that should occur when the <effect> resolves. <content> extends <property>. It consists of one or more event descriptions (e.g., deal damage, draw cards, gain <resource>s, move <token>s, change <state>s, destroy <piece>s). During the <resolve> phase, these descriptions are instantiated as real <event>s and applied to the game state. <content> and <cost> together form a complete <effect>: <cost> executes first, <content> follows. <content> may be empty, but <cost> and <content> must not both be empty.

description.zh: 此效果内容作用的目标规范——描述「效果作用于谁」。target 是抽象的类型规约，具体实例在实际游戏中被触发后才由玩家选择或规则指定。典型结构：对一名敌人 { "scope": "enemy", "count": 1 }、对自己 { "scope": "self" }、对任意玩家 { "scope": "any_player" }、对目标生物 { "scope": "target_creature" }、对全体敌人 { "scope": "all_enemies" }。「抽2张牌」这类效果——抽牌动作的执行者就是效果的受益者，target = { "scope": "self" }。程序根据 target.scope 确定选择范围（如 enemy 枚举所有敌方 Player，self 固定为效果发起者），count 控制选择数量。
description.en: The target specification for this effect content — describes 'who or what the effect acts upon'. target is an abstract type specification; the concrete instance is chosen by the player or determined by rules only when the effect fires in an actual game. Typical structures: one enemy { "scope": "enemy", "count": 1 }, self { "scope": "self" }, any player { "scope": "any_player" }, target creature { "scope": "target_creature" }, all enemies { "scope": "all_enemies" }. For effects like 'draw 2 cards' — the executor of the draw is the beneficiary, target = { "scope": "self" }. The program uses target.scope to determine the selection pool (e.g., enemy enumerates all opposing Players, self is fixed to the effect initiator), and count controls how many to select.

description.zh: 此效果内容的参数。描述效果的具体行为——对 target 做什么。典型结构：造成伤害 { "damage": 2 }、抽牌 { "draw": 3 }、获取资源 { "gain": { "gold": 1 } }、移动 { "move": { "from": "hand", "to": "discard_pile" } }、改变状态 { "set_state": "tapped" }。注意 target 已独立为必填字段，params 仅描述动作本身。程序根据 params 的内容构造对应的 Event 并执行。复合 Content（一次效果做多件事）通过 params 内部结构表达。
description.en: Parameters for this effect content. Describes the specific action — what to do to the target. Typical structures: deal damage { "damage": 2 }, draw cards { "draw": 3 }, gain resources { "gain": { "gold": 1 } }, move { "move": { "from": "hand", "to": "discard_pile" } }, change state { "set_state": "tapped" }. Note: target is a separate required field; params describes only the action itself. The program constructs and executes corresponding Events based on params. Compound Content (one effect does multiple things) is expressed through params' internal structure.

description.zh: 效果内容作用的目标规范——描述「效果作用于谁」。是抽象的类型规约（如 { scope: "enemy", count: 1 }），具体实例在实际游戏触发后才由玩家选择或规则指定。
description.en: Target specification for this effect content — describes 'who the effect acts upon'. An abstract spec; the concrete instance is chosen by the player or determined by rules only at runtime.

description.zh: 效果的具体行为参数——对 target 做什么。如造成伤害 { damage: 2 }、抽牌 { draw: 3 }、获取资源 { gain: { gold: 1 } }。程序根据 params 构造对应的 Event 并执行。
description.en: Parameters describing the specific action — what to do to the target. E.g., deal damage, draw cards, gain resources. The program constructs and executes corresponding Events based on params.

definition.zh: 指明在满足特定条件时将要发生的代价与结果的完整规格。<effect> 继承自 <property>。由 <cost> 和 <content> 两个内部组成部分构成——<cost> 定义触发前必须履行的代价，<content> 定义结算时应发生的具体事件。<cost> 和 <content> 可以有一个为空（免费效果或纯代价效果），但不可同时为空。<effect> 是 <piece> 的核心——<piece> 之所以是 <piece> 而非 <token>，正因为它携带 <effect> 并可被 <play>。<effect> 的运行时生命周期：静默（dormant）→ 被 <activation> 激活（pending）→ 经由 <resolve> 结算，<content> 实例化为真实 <event> 应用到游戏状态。
definition.en: A complete specification of the cost and result that will occur when certain conditions are met. <effect> extends <property>. It consists of two internal components — <cost> defines what must be fulfilled before triggering, <content> defines the specific events that occur during resolution. <cost> and <content> may have one empty (free effect or pure-cost effect), but must not both be empty. <effect> is the core of a <piece> — the reason a <piece> is a <piece> rather than a <token> is precisely that it carries an <effect> and can be <play>ed. Runtime lifecycle: dormant → activated by <activation> (pending) → resolved via <resolve>, where <content> is instantiated as real <event>s and applied to game state.

description.zh: 触发此效果前必须履行的代价。null = 免费效果（如「回合开始时抽一张牌」）。
description.en: The cost that must be fulfilled before triggering this effect. null = free effect (e.g., 'draw a card at the start of your turn').

description.zh: 此效果结算时应发生的具体事件。null = 纯代价效果，Content 的价值由 Piece 自身或游戏规则隐式提供。两种常见情形：(1) Piece 自身的属性或能力已经值回 Cost——例如支付 5 点生命值打出一张高战力生物牌，「获得一个高战力生物」由 Piece 进入 Development Area 这一事实完成；(2) 规则赋予的隐性 Content——例如某 Piece 本身没有效果，但集齐一定数量即获胜，此时 Content 由 Victory Condition 提供，不在 Piece 自身定义。注意：Cost 和 Content 不可同时为 null。
description.en: The specific events that should occur when this effect resolves. null = pure-cost effect, where Content's value is implicitly provided by the Piece itself or by game rules. Two common cases: (1) the Piece's own oversized stats or abilities already justify the Cost — e.g., paying 5 life to play a high-power creature, where 'gain a high-power creature' is accomplished by the Piece entering the Development Area; (2) rules-granted implicit Content — e.g., a Piece has no effect on its own, but collecting a certain number wins the game; the Content is provided by the Victory Condition, not the Piece itself. Note: Cost and Content must not both be null.

description.zh: 触发此 Effect 前必须履行的代价。null 表示免费效果（如「回合开始时抽一张牌」）。与 <content> 不可同时为 null。
description.en: The cost that must be fulfilled before triggering this Effect. null = free effect. Must not be null simultaneously with <content>.

description.zh: 此 Effect 结算时应发生的具体事件。null 表示 Content 由 Piece 自身或游戏规则隐式提供。与 <cost> 不可同时为 null。
description.en: The specific events that should occur when this Effect resolves. null = implicitly provided by Piece or rules. Must not be null simultaneously with <cost>.

definition.zh: 一种在结算后立即执行完毕、不产生持续影响的<content>。<instant_effect>继承自<content>——它是「效果内容」的一种形态。是最常见的效果内容——「获得 2 金币」「抽一张牌」「造成 3 点伤害」均为<instant_effect>。生命周期：对应的<effect>被<activation>激活后，<instant_effect>经<resolve>一次性执行其<params>所描述的事件到<target>，随后终止。与<continuous_content>的对偶：<instant_effect>是一次性的（fire and forget），<continuous_content>是持续性的（always on）。
definition.en: A <content> that executes once upon resolution and produces no ongoing effect. <instant_effect> extends <content> — it is a form of 'effect content'. The most common content form — 'gain 2 gold', 'draw a card', 'deal 3 damage' are all <instant_effect>s. Lifecycle: after the containing <effect> is activated via <activation>, <instant_effect> is <resolve>d — its <params> are executed once against its <target>, then it terminates. Counterpart to <continuous_content>: <instant_effect> is fire-and-forget, <continuous_content> is always-on.

definition.zh: 一种在结算后持续生效、持续修改游戏规则或状态的<content>。<continuous_content>继承自<content>——它是「效果内容」的一种形态。与<instant_effect>的核心区别：<instant_effect>执行一次后结束，<continuous_content>只要来源<piece>在正确的<zone>中就持续生效、无需反复激活。典型例子：「你的所有生物获得+1力量」「蓝牌费用-1」「每回合额外抽一张牌」均为<continuous_content>。<continuous_content>通常不经过<activation>——当来源<piece>进入指定的<zone>（如<development_area>）时自动开始生效，离开时自动失效。对应的<effect>的<cost>通常为 null（被动生效，无需支付代价）。<continuous_content>从<content>继承了<target>和<params>——<target>指明效果持续作用于谁，<params>描述持续修改的内容。
definition.en: A <content> that persists after resolution and continuously modifies game rules or state. <continuous_content> extends <content> — it is a form of 'effect content'. Core difference from <instant_effect>: <instant_effect> executes once and ends; <continuous_content> remains active as long as the source <piece> is in the correct <zone>, without repeated activation. Typical examples: 'all your creatures gain +1 power', 'blue cards cost 1 less', 'draw an extra card each turn'. <continuous_content> typically does not go through <activation> — it automatically takes effect when the source <piece> enters the designated <zone> (e.g., <development_area>) and deactivates when it leaves. The containing <effect>'s <cost> is usually null (passive, no cost to maintain). <continuous_content> inherits <target> and <params> from <content> — <target> specifies who the effect continuously applies to, <params> describes the ongoing modification.

definition.zh: <action> 的内部组成部分之一——<player> 在执行 <action> 时宣告的选择内容。<declaration> 继承自 <property>。玩家必须明确声明他选择做什么、选择哪些目标、以何种方式执行。与 <trigger> 互补构成完整的 <action>：<declaration> 定义玩家选择什么，<trigger> 定义规则如何响应。
definition.en: An internal component of an <action> — the choice content declared by the <player> when executing the <action>. <declaration> extends <property>. The player must explicitly declare what they choose to do, which targets they select, and in what manner. Together with <trigger>, it forms a complete <action>: <declaration> defines what the player chooses, <trigger> defines how the rules respond.

description.zh: 此声明的参数——描述玩家选择了什么、选择了多少、选择了哪些目标。内容由具体的 <action> 类型决定。如「拿取 3 颗不同色宝石」：{ "count": 3, "colors": ["blue", "green", "red"] }。程序根据 params 验证玩家选择的合法性，随后交给 <trigger> 执行对应的规则响应。
description.en: Parameters for this declaration — describes what the player chose, how many, and which targets. Content is determined by the specific <action> type. E.g., 'take 3 different-colored gems': { "count": 3, "colors": ["blue", "green", "red"] }. The program validates the choice based on params, then hands off to <trigger> for rule response execution.

description.zh: 此 Declaration 的具体参数。描述玩家选择了什么——没有 params，Declaration 就是空壳，规则无法知道玩家到底做了什么选择。
description.en: Specific parameters of this Declaration. Describes what the player chose — without params, the declaration is an empty shell and the rules cannot know what choice was made.

definition.zh: 决定游戏 <object> 或 <zone> 的信息可以被哪些 <player> 观察，以及这种观察是强制的还是可选的规则。<information_visibility> 继承自 <property>。定义了五种基本状态：Public（公开，必须对所有玩家可见）、Private（私有，仅拥有者可观察且不可公开）、Protected（保护，拥有者可选择是否向其他玩家临时展示）、Partially Public（部分公开，仅部分内容对全员可见）、Hidden（隐藏，所有玩家均不可观察）。可在游戏过程中被 <effect> 改变——一张面朝下的卡被翻转后，其可见性从 Hidden 变为 Public。
definition.en: A rule that determines which <player>s can observe the information of a game <object> or <zone>, and whether such observation is mandatory or optional. <information_visibility> extends <property>. It defines five basic states: Public (must be visible to all players), Private (only the owner can observe, cannot be shared), Protected (owner may choose to temporarily reveal to others), Partially Public (only part of the content is visible to all), Hidden (no player can observe). Can be changed during gameplay by <effect>s — a face-down card flipped face-up changes from Hidden to Public.

public.zh: 公开——所有 <player> 均可无条件观察此信息。游戏规则强制此信息对所有玩家可见，不可隐藏。
public.en: Public — all <player>s can observe this information unconditionally. Game rules mandate this information be visible to all players and cannot be hidden.

private.zh: 私有——仅拥有此信息的 <player> 可观察，且不可主动向其他 <player> 公开。其他玩家无法通过任何合法手段获知此信息的内容。
private.en: Private — only the <player> who owns this information can observe it, and they cannot voluntarily reveal it to other <player>s. Other players have no legitimate means to learn its content.

protected.zh: 保护——拥有此信息的 <player> 可观察，且可选择是否在特定时刻向其他 <player> 临时展示。展示行为由拥有者主动控制，展示后信息自动恢复为仅拥有者可观察。
protected.en: Protected — the <player> who owns this information can observe it and may choose to temporarily reveal it to other <player>s at specific moments. Revelation is actively controlled by the owner; after revelation, the information automatically returns to owner-only visibility.

partially_public.zh: 部分公开——一个信息集合中，一部分对所有 <player> 可见，其余部分为私有或隐藏。这涵盖两种典型场景：(1) 单一实体内部的部分可见——如一张卡牌的费用公开但效果文本隐藏，或卡牌背面全员可见而正面内容私有；(2) 集合中部分实体可见、部分不可见——如一个牌堆仅最顶上一张正面翻出（全员可见），其余全部背面朝下（隐藏）。核心判定标准：信息集合整体不被完全暴露，存在可见子集与不可见子集的边界。
partially_public.en: Partially public — within a collection of information, one part is visible to all <player>s while the rest is private or hidden. This covers two typical scenarios: (1) partial visibility within a single entity — e.g., a card's cost is public but its effect text is hidden, or a card's back is visible to all while its front content is private; (2) some entities in a collection are visible while others are not — e.g., a deck where only the top card is face-up (visible to all) and all others are face-down (hidden). The core criterion: the information collection as a whole is not fully exposed; there exists a boundary between the visible subset and the invisible subset.

hidden.zh: 隐藏——所有 <player> 均不可观察此信息。信息存在于游戏状态中但不对任何玩家暴露，通常用于随机化组件（如牌堆顶部的未知卡牌）或尚未揭晓的游戏内容。
hidden.en: Hidden — no <player> can observe this information. The information exists in the game state but is exposed to no one, typically used for randomized components (e.g., unknown cards on top of a deck) or unrevealed game content.

definition.zh: 具有明确开始与结束边界的执行单元。<procedure> 是游戏流程的骨架——它定义了「游戏现在处于什么阶段」「接下来该做什么」。嵌套是自由形式的：<round> 里可以有 <phase>，<phase> 里可以有 <round>，<turn> 里可以有 <phase>，一整局游戏本身也可以视为一个 <round>。没有固定的层级，具体嵌套关系由每款游戏的规则决定。所有 <procedure> 子类（<round>、<turn>、<phase> 等）共享同一套字段，区别仅在于语义，不在结构。
definition.en: An execution unit with clear start and end boundaries. <procedure> is the skeleton of game flow. Nesting is free-form: a <round> can contain <phase>s, a <phase> can contain <round>s, a <turn> can contain <phase>s, and an entire game can itself be a <round>. There is no fixed hierarchy — the nesting is determined by each game's rules. All <procedure> subclasses (<round>, <turn>, <phase>, etc.) share the same fields; they differ only in semantics, not structure.

description.zh: 此流程的进入条件。定义了「什么情况发生时，此流程被激活」。可以是一个 Condition（如「所有玩家完成行动后」），也可以是一个 Trigger（如「回合标记重置时」）。当此条件满足时，程序将执行权移入此 Procedure。
description.en: The entry condition for this procedure. Defines 'when does this procedure become active'. Can be a Condition or a Trigger. When met, the program transfers execution into this Procedure.

description.zh: 此流程的退出条件。定义了「什么情况发生时，此流程终止」。当此条件满足时，程序将执行权从本 Procedure 移出，交给下一个 Procedure 或父级 Procedure。如果是循环型 Procedure（如 Round），end 条件触发后可能回到自身的 start，形成循环。
description.en: The exit condition for this procedure. Defines 'when does this procedure terminate'. When met, the program transfers execution out of this Procedure. For cyclical Procedures (e.g. a Round), the end condition may loop back to its own start, forming a cycle.

description.zh: 嵌套在此流程内部的子流程。子流程在当前 <procedure> 激活后按游戏规则定义的顺序执行。<round>、<turn>、<phase> 可以任意嵌套——一个 <phase> 里可能包含多个 <round>，一个 <turn> 里可能有多个 <phase>。若为空，表示此 <procedure> 是叶子节点，直接包含 <action> 而非子流程。
description.en: Child procedures nested within this procedure. Executed in the order defined by game rules while the parent is active. <round>, <turn>, and <phase> can nest in any arrangement — a <phase> may contain multiple <round>s, a <turn> may contain multiple <phase>s. If empty, this is a leaf <procedure> that contains Actions directly.

description.zh: Procedure 的唯一标识符。用于在规则中精确引用特定流程实例，管理流程间的嵌套和跳转关系。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Procedure. Used to precisely reference a specific procedure instance and manage nesting and transitions.

description.zh: 此 Procedure 的进入条件——什么情况发生时此流程被激活。可以是 <condition> 或 Trigger。定义「什么时候开始」。
description.en: Entry condition for this Procedure — when does it become active. Can be a <condition> or Trigger. Defines 'when to start'.

description.zh: 此 Procedure 的退出条件——什么情况发生时此流程终止。循环型 Procedure 的 end 可能回到自身的 start，形成循环。定义「什么时候结束」。
description.en: Exit condition for this Procedure — when does it terminate. For cyclical Procedures, the end may loop back to start. Defines 'when to end'.

description.zh: 嵌套在此 Procedure 内部的子流程。空数组表示叶子节点，直接包含 <action> 而非子流程。<round>、<turn>、<phase> 可任意嵌套。
description.en: Child Procedures nested within this one. Empty means a leaf node containing <action>s directly. <round>, <turn>, <phase> can nest freely.

definition.zh: 游戏程序结构中一个完整的、可重复的循环单元。<round> 继承自 <procedure>。一轮内部结构固定——每次循环执行相同的 <phase> 序列。一整局游戏本身就是一个最外层的 <round>（「再来一局」=「再来一轮」）。<round> 的 children 只能是 <phase>：<round> 不直接包含 <turn> 或另一个 <round>，它通过 <phase> 间接组织下级流程。
definition.en: A complete, repeatable cycle in game procedure structure. <round> extends <procedure>. Its internal structure is fixed — each cycle executes the same sequence of <phase>s. An entire game is itself an outermost <round>. A <round>'s children can only be <phase>s: a <round> does not directly contain <turn>s or other <round>s; it organizes lower-level flow indirectly through <phase>s.

description.zh: 此轮包含的阶段序列。每轮按此顺序执行各 <phase>。仅允许 <phase> 类型的 <procedure> 作为直接子节点。
description.en: The sequence of Phases in this round. Each cycle executes Phases in this order. Only <phase>-type <procedure>s are allowed as direct children.

description.zh: 此 Round 包含的 <phase> 序列。每轮按此顺序执行各 Phase。仅允许 <phase> 作为直接子节点。
description.en: The sequence of <phase>s in this Round. Each cycle executes Phases in this order. Only <phase>s are allowed as direct children.

definition.zh: 将排他的行动权授予单一 <player> 的执行单元。<turn> 继承自 <procedure>。同一时刻至多一个 <turn> 处于激活状态。<turn> 的 children 只能是 <phase>——即使是「玩家选择一个行动」这种简单场景，也隐含了一个「选择行动阶段」。<turn> 不直接包含 <action>，它通过 <phase> 定义玩家在此回合内可以做什么。
definition.en: An execution unit that grants exclusive action rights to a single <player>. <turn> extends <procedure>. At most one <turn> is active at any given moment. A <turn>'s children can only be <phase>s — even a simple 'player chooses an action' scenario implicitly contains a 'choose action phase'. A <turn> does not directly contain <action>s; it defines what a player can do during this turn through its <phase>s.

description.zh: 此回合包含的阶段序列。仅允许 <phase> 类型的 <procedure> 作为直接子节点。
description.en: The sequence of Phases in this turn. Only <phase>-type <procedure>s are allowed as direct children.

description.zh: 此 Turn 包含的 <phase> 序列。仅允许 <phase> 作为直接子节点。空数组表示此 Turn 直接包含 Action。
description.en: The sequence of <phase>s in this Turn. Only <phase>s are allowed as direct children.

definition.zh: 游戏流程中，合法动作集合保持一致、规则上下文不发生强制切换的持续区间。<phase> 继承自 <procedure>。是唯一承载「规则上下文」的 <procedure>——当前 <phase> 决定了哪些 <action> 合法、哪些 <effect> 生效。不强制绑定 <player>，允许完全的自动机阶段（无人阶段，仅有 <trigger> 驱动）。<phase> 的 children 可以是 <round>、<turn> 或另一个 <phase>，也可以是叶子节点（直接包含 <action> 列表）。
definition.en: A continuous interval in game flow where the set of legal actions remains consistent and the rule context does not switch. <phase> extends <procedure>. It is the only <procedure> that carries 'rule context' — the current <phase> determines which <action>s are legal and which <effect>s are active. Not required to bind to a <player>, allowing fully automated phases (player-less, driven only by <trigger>s). A <phase>'s children can be <round>s, <turn>s, other <phase>s, or it can be a leaf node containing an <action> list directly.

description.zh: 此阶段包含的子流程。可以包含 <round>、<turn>、<phase> 任意组合。若为空，此 <phase> 为叶子节点——直接暴露一组合法 <action> 供玩家选择（或完全由 Trigger 自动驱动）。
description.en: Child procedures within this phase. Can contain any combination of <round>s, <turn>s, or <phase>s. If empty, this is a leaf <phase> — it directly exposes a set of legal Actions for the player to choose from (or is fully driven by Triggers).

description.zh: 此阶段内玩家可执行的 <action> 列表。仅当 children 为空（叶子 <phase>）时此字段有意义——它定义了当前规则上下文中的合法行动。非叶子 <phase> 的合法 <action> 由其子流程决定。
description.en: The list of Actions a player can execute during this phase. Only meaningful when children is empty (leaf Phase) — it defines the legal actions in the current rule context. Non-leaf Phases derive their legal actions from their children.

description.zh: 此 Phase 包含的子流程——可以是 <round>、<turn>、<phase> 任意组合。若为空，此 Phase 为叶子节点，直接暴露一组合法 <action>。
description.en: Child Procedures within this Phase — can be any combination of <round>s, <turn>s, <phase>s. If empty, this is a leaf Phase exposing legal <action>s directly.

description.zh: 此 Phase 内玩家可执行的 <action> 列表。仅当 children 为空（叶子 Phase）时此字段有意义——它定义了当前规则上下文中的合法行动。
description.en: The list of <action>s available during this Phase. Only meaningful when children is empty (leaf Phase) — it defines the legal actions in the current rule context.

definition.zh: <object> 在 <zone> 之间移动或 <ownership> 变更的 <event>。<transfer> 继承自 <event>。
definition.en: An <event> where an <object> moves between <zone>s or its <ownership> changes. <transfer> extends <event>.

description.zh: <object> 移出的源 <zone>。必须是游戏中已定义的一个 <zone> 实例。
description.en: The <zone> the <object> moves from. Must be a defined <zone> instance.

description.zh: <object> 移入的目标 <zone>。可以是另一个 <zone>，也可以与 source 相同（如区域内重排序）。
description.en: The destination <zone> the <object> moves to. May differ from source or be the same (e.g. reordering within a <zone>).

description.zh: 被移动的 <object>。指向游戏中一个具体的 <object> 实例。同时承担 <event> 中 target 的语义——此 <object> 就是该转移事件所作用的目标。
description.en: The <object> being moved. References a concrete <object> instance. Also fulfills the <event> target semantics — this <object> is what the transfer event acts upon.

description.zh: 是否同时改变 <ownership>。若为 true，则 destination <zone> 关联的 <player> 成为新所有者。
description.en: Whether <ownership> also changes. If true, the <player> associated with the destination <zone> becomes the new owner.

description.zh: 转移的 <object> 数量。<token>（可互换）可能 > 1；<piece>（不可互换）通常 = 1。
description.en: Quantity of <object>s transferred. <token>s (interchangeable) may be > 1; <piece>s (unique) are usually = 1.

description.zh: <object> 移出的源 <zone>。必须是游戏中已定义的一个 <zone> 实例。没有 source，转移无从发生。
description.en: The <zone> the <object> moves from. Must be a defined <zone> instance. Without a source, the transfer cannot occur.

description.zh: <object> 移入的目标 <zone>。可以是另一个 <zone>，也可以与 source 相同（如区域内重排序）。
description.en: The destination <zone> the <object> moves to. May differ from source or be the same (e.g., reordering within a <zone>).

description.zh: 被移动的 <object>。同时承担 <event> 中 target 的语义——此 <object> 就是该转移事件所作用的目标。
description.en: The <object> being moved. Also fulfills the <event> target semantics — this <object> is what the transfer event acts upon.

description.zh: 是否同时改变 <ownership>。若为 true，destination <zone> 关联的 <player> 成为新所有者。默认 false。
description.en: Whether <ownership> also changes. If true, the <player> associated with the destination <zone> becomes the new owner. Default false.

description.zh: 转移的 <object> 数量。<token>（可互换）可能大于 1；<piece>（不可互换）通常为 1。默认 1。
description.en: Quantity of <object>s transferred. <token>s (interchangeable) may be > 1; <piece>s (unique) are usually 1. Default 1.

definition.zh: 由 <player> 主动发起的 <event>，它是对游戏规则说「我选择做这件事」的声明。<action> 继承自 <event>，由两个互补部分组成——<declaration> 定义玩家选择什么，<trigger> 定义规则如何响应。二者绑定关系是结构性的：每个 <action> 必定绑定一个 <trigger>。<action> 本身不直接改变游戏状态——玩家做出选择后，规则通过 <trigger> 启动后续 <event>（<transfer>、<state> 变更等）。<action> 的合法性由当前 <phase> 的规则上下文决定。
definition.en: An <event> actively initiated by a <player>. It is a declaration to the game rules: 'I choose to do this'. <action> extends <event> and consists of two complementary parts — <declaration> defines what the player chooses, <trigger> defines how the rules respond. Their binding is structural: every <action> is necessarily bound to a <trigger>. An <action> does not directly change game state — after the player makes a choice, the rules launch follow-up <event>s (<transfer>, <state> changes, etc.) through the <trigger>. The legality of an <action> is determined by the current <phase>'s rule context.

description.zh: 从 <event> 继承，此处窄化：<action> 的执行者始终是一个 <player>，不可为 null。每个 <action> 必有一个做出决策的玩家——这正是 <action> 与 <trigger> 的本质区别。
description.en: Inherited from <event>, narrowed here: the executor of an <action> is always a <player>, never null. Every <action> has a decision-making player — this is the essential difference between an <action> and a <trigger>.

description.zh: 此 <action> 中玩家宣告的选择内容。<declaration> 描述「玩家选择了做什么」——选择了哪些目标、以何种方式。与 <trigger> 互补：<declaration> 是玩家的选择输出，<trigger> 是规则的响应输入。
description.en: The choice content declared by the player in this <action>. <declaration> describes 'what the player chose to do' — which targets, in what manner. Complementary to <trigger>: <declaration> is the player's choice output, <trigger> is the rules' response input.

description.zh: 此 <action> 必定绑定的 <trigger>。玩家做出 <declaration> 后，规则通过此 <trigger> 启动对应的后续 <event>（<transfer>、<state> 变更等）。每个 <action> 必有一个 <trigger>——这是结构性必然：规则不可能因为玩家选择了某个行动就「自动知道该做什么」，必须有一个 <trigger> 承接这个选择并调度后续效果。
description.en: The <trigger> necessarily bound to this <action>. After the player makes a <declaration>, the rules launch corresponding follow-up <event>s (<transfer>, <state> changes, etc.) through this <trigger>. Every <action> must have a <trigger> — this is structurally necessary: the rules cannot 'automatically know what to do' just because a player chose an action; a <trigger> must take the choice and dispatch the subsequent effects.

description.zh: 执行此 <action> 的 <player>。从 <event> 继承并窄化：<action> 的 actor 始终是一个 <player>，不可为 null。
description.en: The <player> executing this <action>. Inherited from <event> and narrowed: an <action>'s actor is always a <player>, never null.

description.zh: 此 <action> 中玩家宣告的选择内容。每个 <action> 必有一个 <declaration>——没有声明，规则无从知道玩家做了什么选择，<trigger> 也无事可响应。
description.en: The choice content declared by the player in this <action>. Every <action> needs a <declaration> — without one, the rules cannot know what the player chose, and the <trigger> has nothing to respond to.

description.zh: 此 <action> 必定绑定的 <trigger>。玩家做出选择后，规则必须有一个承接点来调度后续效果——这正是 <action> 的「声明」本质：<action> 只负责宣布选择，<trigger> 负责执行效果。
description.en: The <trigger> necessarily bound to this <action>. After the player chooses, the rules must have a receiving point to dispatch subsequent effects — this reflects the declarative nature of <action>: <action> announces the choice, <trigger> executes the effects.

definition.zh: 标记游戏终局流程启动的 <condition>。<endgame_condition> 继承自 <condition>——结构上与普通 <condition> 无异，区别仅在于语义角色：当此 <condition> 评估为 true 时，游戏进入终局流程。终局流程的具体行为由游戏规则定义——可能是立即终止（如「<deck> 被抽空时游戏立刻结束」），也可能先执行一个收尾阶段（如「触发后所有 <player> 补完当前 <round> 再结算」）。典型触发条件：「任意 <player> 达到 10 分」「最后一张 <card> 被抽走」「所有 <tile> 放置完毕」。一局游戏可以有多个 <endgame_condition>——任一满足即触发终局流程。
definition.en: A <condition> that marks the start of the endgame process. <endgame_condition> extends <condition> — structurally identical to an ordinary <condition>, differing only in its semantic role: when this <condition> evaluates to true, the game enters its endgame process. What happens during endgame is defined by the specific game's rules — it could be immediate termination (e.g., 'game ends instantly when the <deck> runs out'), or a wrap-up phase first (e.g., 'all <player>s finish the current <round> before final scoring'). Typical trigger conditions: 'any <player> reaches 10 points', 'the last <card> is drawn', 'all <tile>s have been placed'. A game may have multiple <endgame_condition>s — satisfying any one triggers the endgame process.

definition.zh: 在终局流程完成后、决定哪位 <player> 胜出的 <condition>。<victory_condition> 继承自 <condition>，其判定标准是一个按优先级排序的 <condition> 序列——按顺序满足条件的 <player>（们）是胜者。判定流程：满足第 1 条 <condition> 的 <player> 为候选胜者；候选多于 1 人时，在候选中继续应用下一条 <condition> 筛选，直到只剩 1 人或序列用完；序列用完仍有多名候选则为平局。与 <endgame_condition> 的分工：<endgame_condition> 回答「游戏何时结束」，<victory_condition> 回答「结束后谁赢」。允许合作胜利（所有 <player> 共同获胜），允许无人获胜（全员失败）。
definition.en: A <condition> that determines which <player> wins, evaluated after the endgame process completes. <victory_condition> extends <condition>, and its adjudication standard is an ordered sequence of <condition>s — the <player>(s) satisfying the criteria in order win. Adjudication: <player>s satisfying the 1st <condition> become winner candidates; if more than one remains, apply the next <condition> to the candidates, continuing until exactly one remains or the sequence is exhausted; if multiple candidates remain after the sequence, the result is a tie. Division of labor with <endgame_condition>: <endgame_condition> answers 'when does the game end', <victory_condition> answers 'who wins after it ends'. Cooperative victories (all <player>s win together) are allowed, as is no winner at all (everyone loses).

description.zh: 胜负判定的条件序列，按优先级从高到低排序。每条<condition>都是对单个<player>求值的判定式（如「声望最高」「发展卡最少」）——允许并列，并列者视为同时满足。判定流程：满足第 1 条的<player>为候选；多于 1 人则在候选中应用下一条继续筛选；直到只剩 1 人或序列用完。
description.en: The ordered sequence of victory criteria, sorted from highest to lowest priority. Each <condition> is a predicate evaluated per <player> (e.g., 'highest prestige', 'fewest development cards') — ties count as satisfied simultaneously. Adjudication: <player>s satisfying the 1st criterion become candidates; if more than one remains, apply the next criterion to the candidates; continue until exactly one remains or the sequence is exhausted.

description.zh: 胜负判定必须给出形式化的条件序列——没有条件序列，程序无法确定胜者。
description.en: Victory adjudication must provide a formalized condition sequence — without it, the program cannot determine the winner.

definition.zh: 游戏规则中负责启动 <event> 的统一机制。<trigger> 继承自 <event>。其角色是「事件调度器」——本质为「timing + condition → events」：时机（timing）到达且此时 <condition> 满足，<trigger> 才触发，启动对应的后续 <event>（如结算 <effect>、执行 <transfer>、改变 <state>）。满足 <condition> 本身不会触发——时机未至，条件持续满足也只是待命；时机到达时条件不满足，同样不触发。一切游戏状态变更最终都由 <trigger> 负责发起。<trigger> 不由任何 <player> 直接控制，而由规则自动响应——触发不以玩家意志为转移，它的 actor 始终为 null。与 <action> 的关系：<action> 是 <trigger> 最常见的触发原因——玩家打出一张牌（<action>），规则自动识别此事件并触发对应的 <trigger>，<trigger> 再启动「支付费用」「获得资源」「造成伤害」等后续 <event>。
definition.en: The unified mechanism in game rules responsible for launching <event>s. <trigger> extends <event>. Its role is that of an 'event dispatcher' — its essence is 'timing + condition → events': when the timing arrives AND the <condition> holds at that moment, the <trigger> fires and launches corresponding follow-up <event>s (e.g., resolving an <effect>, executing a <transfer>, changing a <state>). Satisfying the <condition> alone does not fire it — before the timing arrives, a continuously satisfied condition merely stands by; if the condition does not hold when the timing arrives, it does not fire either. All game state changes are ultimately initiated by a <trigger>. A <trigger> is not directly controlled by any <player> — it responds automatically to the rules, firing regardless of player will, and its actor is always null. Relationship with <action>: <action> is the most common cause of <trigger> firing — a player plays a card (<action>), the rules automatically recognize this event and fire the corresponding <trigger>, which then launches follow-up <event>s such as 'pay cost', 'gain resource', 'deal damage'.

description.zh: 从 <event> 继承，此处窄化为 null：<trigger> 不由任何 <player> 主动发起，没有执行者。这正是 <trigger> 与 <action> 的本质区别。
description.en: Inherited from <event>, narrowed here to null: a <trigger> is not initiated by any <player> and has no executor. This is the essential difference between a <trigger> and an <action>.

description.zh: <trigger> 的触发时机——<condition> 的检查钟声。时机到达且此时 <condition> 满足，<trigger> 才触发。时机可以是：某个状态变化的瞬间（「任何使宝石总数变化的 <event> 结算完成时」）、阶段边界（「一名 <player> 的回合结束时」）、或某个 <event> 完成后（「此 <action> 执行完毕时」）。满足 <condition> 不代表立即触发——时机未至，条件满足只是待命；时机到达时条件不满足则不触发。
description.en: The firing timing of the <trigger> — the bell that prompts the <condition> check. The <trigger> fires only when the timing arrives AND the <condition> holds at that moment. A timing can be: the instant of a state change ('when any <event> that changes the gem total finishes resolving'), a phase boundary ('when a <player>'s turn ends'), or the completion of some <event> ('when this <action> finishes executing'). Satisfying the <condition> does not mean firing immediately — before the timing arrives, a satisfied condition merely stands by; if the condition does not hold when the timing arrives, it does not fire.

description.zh: 触发本 <trigger> 所需满足的 <condition>——一个纯粹的状态事实（如「宝石总数 >10」「某 <noble> 的 requirement 被满足」），不包含时机描述（时机由 timing 字段表达）。<trigger> 的本质即「timing + condition → events」。每一个 <trigger> 都必须有 <condition>，即使是被 <action> 触发的 <trigger>——「此 <action> 的 precondition 满足且 <declaration> 合法」本身就是 <condition>。
description.en: The <condition> that must hold for this <trigger> to fire — a pure state fact (e.g., 'gem total >10', 'a <noble>'s requirement is met'), containing no timing description (timing is expressed by the timing field). The essence of a <trigger> is 'timing + condition → events'. Every <trigger> must have a <condition> — even for <action>-bound <trigger>s, 'this <action>'s precondition is met and its <declaration> is legal' is itself the <condition>.

description.zh: <trigger> 被触发后启动的后续 <event> 列表。元素可以是任意 <event> 子类：<transfer>、<play>、<resolve>、<state> 变更等。例如「购买」<action> 的 <trigger> 含两个 <event>：一次 <transfer>（支付费用）和一次 <play>（卡牌入场）。每个 <event> 可声明 `do_after` 字段引用其他 <event> 的 id，表示必须等被引用的 <event> 完成后才能执行；无 `do_after` 的 <event> 互相独立，可任意顺序或并行执行。为了支持 `do_after`，每个可能需要被引用的 <event> 都应声明 `id`。
description.en: The list of follow-up <event>s launched after the <trigger> fires. Elements may be any <event> subclass: <transfer>, <play>, <resolve>, <state> changes, etc. For example, a 'purchase' <action>'s <trigger> contains two <event>s: a <transfer> (paying the cost) and a <play> (the card entering play). Each <event> may declare a `do_after` field referencing another <event>'s id, meaning it must wait for the referenced <event> to complete; <event>s without `do_after` are independent of each other and may execute in any order or in parallel. To support `do_after`, every <event> that might be referenced should declare an `id`.

description.zh: 每一个 <trigger> 都必须声明触发时机——满足 <condition> 不代表立即触发，时机到达且条件满足才触发。没有 <timing> 的 <trigger> 无法确定何时检查条件。
description.en: Every <trigger> must declare its firing timing — satisfying the <condition> does not mean firing immediately; it fires only when the timing arrives and the condition holds. A <trigger> without <timing> cannot determine when to check its condition.

description.zh: 每一个 <trigger> 都必须有触发条件——即使是被 <action> 触发的 <trigger>，「此 <action> 的 precondition 满足且 <declaration> 合法」本身就是 <condition>。没有 <condition> 的 <trigger> 无法确定能否触发。
description.en: Every <trigger> must have a firing condition — even for <action>-bound <trigger>s, 'this <action>'s precondition is met and its <declaration> is legal' is itself the <condition>. A <trigger> without a <condition> cannot determine whether to fire.

description.zh: <trigger> 的职责是启动后续 <event>——没有 <event> 列表的 <trigger> 是空调度器。此约束要求子类声明被触发后执行哪些 <event>。
description.en: A <trigger>'s job is to launch follow-up <event>s — a <trigger> without an <event> list is an empty dispatcher. This constraint requires subclasses to declare which <event>s execute upon firing.

definition.zh: 将一个已被激活的 <effect> 的 <content> 实际应用到游戏 <state> 的 <event>。<resolve> 继承自 <event>。它是 <effect> 生命周期的最后一步：<trigger> 激活 <effect>（进入 pending 状态后），<resolve> 将 <content> 中描述的事件描述实例化为真实的 <event>（如 <transfer>、<state> 变更等）并执行。结算完毕后，该 <effect> 回归静默（dormant）或从游戏中移除。<resolve> 本身是规则自动执行的——actor 为 null。
definition.en: An <event> that actually applies the <content> of an activated <effect> to the game <state>. <resolve> extends <event>. It is the final step of the <effect> lifecycle: after a <trigger> activates the <effect> (placing it in pending state), <resolve> instantiates the event descriptions in <content> as real <event>s (e.g., <transfer>s, <state> changes, etc.) and executes them. After resolution, the <effect> returns to dormant state or is removed from the game. <resolve> is automatically executed by the rules — its actor is null.

description.zh: <resolve> 的本质是将 <content> 实例化为真实的 <event> 并应用到游戏状态——没有 <content>，<resolve> 无事可做。此约束要求子类提供一份可结算的 <content>，指明结算时应发生哪些具体事件。
description.en: The essence of <resolve> is instantiating <content> as real <event>s and applying them to game state — without <content>, <resolve> has nothing to do. This constraint requires subclasses to provide a resolvable <content> specifying what concrete events should occur during resolution.

definition.zh: 对某个 <zone>（通常为 <deck> 类型 <reserve>）中全部或部分 <object> 的顺序进行随机重排的 <event>。<shuffle> 继承自 <event>。其结果是使 <object> 的排列从当前已知或可推测的顺序变为不可预测的顺序，同时将该 <zone> 的信息状态从 Partially Public 重置为 Hidden。<shuffle> 可由 <player> 作为 <action> 的一部分主动执行（actor 为 <player>），也可由规则通过 <trigger> 自动要求（actor 为 null）——例如「每当 <discard_pile> 被洗入 <deck> 时自动洗混」。
definition.en: An <event> that randomly reorders all or some <object>s in a <zone> (typically a <deck>-type <reserve>). <shuffle> extends <event>. Its result is transitioning the object ordering from a known or inferable sequence to an unpredictable one, while resetting the <zone>'s information state from Partially Public to Hidden. <shuffle> may be actively performed by a <player> as part of an <action> (actor is <player>), or automatically required by rules via a <trigger> (actor is null) — e.g., 'shuffle automatically whenever the <discard_pile> is merged into the <deck>'.

description.zh: 从 <event> 继承，此处窄化为 <zone>：被洗混的目标区域。通常为 <deck> 类型 <reserve>，该 <zone> 中的 <object> 顺序将被随机重排。
description.en: Inherited from <event>, narrowed here to <zone>: the target zone being shuffled. Typically a <deck>-type <reserve>, whose <object> ordering will be randomly rearranged.

definition.zh: 一种用于存放游戏组件的存储型 <zone>。<reserve> 继承自 <zone>，abstract。核心语义是「存放备用」——游戏物件在此被汇集、叠放或陈列，作为游戏物资的库存。物件在 <reserve> 中处于「备用」状态，直到被抽取、购买或以其他方式移入使用中。典型的 <reserve> 子类包括：<supply>（直接取用的可计数存储池；<ownership> 为 null 时是公共供应堆，指向特定 <player> 时是玩家供应堆）、<market>（待获取 <piece> 的陈列区）、<deck>（按序抽取的叠放区）、<pool>（随机化组件的存储区）。
definition.en: A storage-type <zone> for holding game components. <reserve> extends <zone>, abstract. Core semantic is 'keeping in storage' — game objects are pooled, stacked, or displayed here as the game's material inventory. Objects in a <reserve> are in a 'reserve' state until drawn, purchased, or otherwise moved into active use. Typical <reserve> subclasses: <supply> (countable direct-take storage pool; public when <ownership> is null, player-specific when <ownership> points to a <player>), <market> (display area of acquirable <piece>s), <deck> (ordered draw stack), <pool> (storage zone for randomizable components).

definition.zh: 存放已使用、已消耗或主动弃置的游戏物件的 <zone>。<discard_pile> 继承自 <zone>。物件离开活跃使用状态后进入弃牌堆——卡牌被使用后弃入、<token> 被消耗后归入、<piece> 被摧毁后置入。通常是面朝上的（全员可见），内容物成为所有玩家的公共信息。在许多游戏中可被重新洗入 <deck> 以实现物件的循环复用。在仅有一叠共用卡牌且使用后即弃入的游戏中，弃牌堆就是 <deck> 的「反面」——一个空了，另一个满到可以洗回来。
definition.en: A <zone> that holds game components that have been used, consumed, or voluntarily discarded. <discard_pile> extends <zone>. Objects enter after leaving active use — cards played and resolved, <token>s consumed, <piece>s destroyed. Typically face-up (visible to all), making its contents public information. In many games it can be reshuffled back into the <deck> to recycle components. In games with a single shared deck, the <discard_pile> is the <deck>'s 'mirror' — when one empties, the other is full enough to shuffle back.

definition.zh: 归属于特定 <player> 的 <zone>，用于存放该玩家个人的游戏组件。<player_zone> 继承自 <zone>，abstract。是 <reserve> 的对偶概念——<reserve> 存放共享的游戏物资，<player_zone> 存放属于单个玩家的东西。owner 始终指向一个 <player> 实例（不可为 null）。典型的子类包括：<player_holding>（玩家手持或暂存的 <piece>）、<development_area>（玩家已打出/建造、正处于活跃使用中的 <piece> 所在区域）。
definition.en: A <zone> that belongs to a specific <player>, holding that player's personal game components. <player_zone> extends <zone>, abstract. It is the counterpart to <reserve> — while <reserve> stores shared game materials, <player_zone> stores what belongs to an individual player. owner is always a <player> reference (never null). Typical subclasses: <player_holding> (where a player keeps <piece>s in hand or temporarily), <development_area> (where a player's played/built <piece>s reside in active use).

description.zh: 从 <zone> 继承，此处窄化：<player_zone> 始终归属于一个 <player>，不可为 null。
description.en: Inherited from <zone>, narrowed here: <player_zone> always belongs to a <player>, never null.

definition.zh: 一种 <piece>，通常为扁平矩形，有正面和背面两个面。<card> 继承自 <piece>。正面承载该卡牌的全部身份信息——名称、费用（<cost>）、效果文本（<effect>）、插画等；背面通常与同 <deck> 中其他卡牌一致，用于隐藏正面信息。卡牌是桌游中最常见的 <piece> 形态，也是 <play> 的主要对象——玩家从手牌（<player_holding> 的子类）中打出卡牌，支付其 <cost>，触发其 <effect>。某些 <card> 可以承载 <zone>——例如 Arkham Horror 的地点牌上面可以放置线索标记，Civolution 的初始芯片牌在设置阶段可以提供容纳目标芯片的 zone。这种 zone 的生命周期绑定在卡牌上——卡牌被移除时，其承载的 zone 也随之消失。
definition.en: A type of <piece>, typically flat and rectangular, with a front face and a back face. <card> extends <piece>. The front face carries the card's full identity — name, <cost>, <effect> text, illustration, etc.; the back face is usually identical across all cards in a <deck>, serving to conceal the front. Cards are the most common <piece> form in board games and the primary target of <play> — players play cards from their hand (a subclass of <player_holding>), pay their <cost>, and trigger their <effect>.
