Some <card>s can host <zone>s — e.g., location cards in Arkham Horror can hold clue tokens, and the starting chip card in Civolution provides a zone for goal chips during setup. Such a zone's lifecycle is bound to the card — when the card is removed, its hosted zone disappears with it.

description.zh: 此卡牌承载的 <zone>。部分卡牌可以充当 zone 的宿主——如 Arkham Horror 地点牌上的线索区、Civolution 初始芯片牌上的目标芯片区。zone 的生命周期绑定在此卡牌上——卡牌被移除时 zone 随之消失。普通卡牌（不承载 zone）可省略此字段。
description.en: The <zone>s hosted on this card. Some cards serve as zone hosts — e.g., the clue zone on Arkham Horror location cards, the goal chip zone on Civolution's starting chip card. The zone's lifecycle is bound to the card — when the card is removed, the zone disappears with it. Omit for ordinary cards that don't host zones.

definition.zh: 一种 <piece>，通常较 <card> 更小更厚，形状不定——六边形、正方形、长方形或不规则形状均有。<tile> 继承自 <piece>。典型例子包括卡坦岛的六角地形板块、卡卡颂的地图板块、Azul 的装饰砖块、多米诺骨牌式拼接板块。
definition.en: A type of <piece>, typically smaller and thicker than a <card>, with variable shapes — hexagonal, square, rectangular, or irregular. <tile> extends <piece>. Typical examples: Catan hexagonal terrain tiles, Carcassonne map tiles, Azul decorative tiles, domino-style placement tiles.

definition.zh: 存放无差别的、可直接取用的 <object> 的 <reserve>。<supply> 继承自 <reserve>。核心语义是「备用且直接取用」——此区域中的 <object> 完全相同且可互相替代（通常为 <token> 或 <resource>），获取方式为直接取用而不需抽取或随机：玩家只决定「取多少」，不决定「取哪个」。对象数量可能有限或无限，不支持顺序操作和洗混。访问权限由 <ownership> 决定：<ownership> 为 null 时是公共供应堆，所有玩家均可取用；<ownership> 为特定 <player> 时是玩家供应堆，仅该玩家可取用。典型例子：璀璨宝石的宝石供应堆、卡坦岛的资源卡供应堆、某些游戏中每位玩家面前分出的资源池。
definition.en: A <reserve> that holds undifferentiated <object>s which can be directly taken. <supply> extends <reserve>. Core semantic is 'kept in storage and directly taken' — objects here are identical and interchangeable (typically <token>s or <resource>s), accessed by direct taking without drawing or randomness: the player only decides 'how many', not 'which one'. Quantity may be limited or unlimited; no ordering or shuffling. Access rights are determined by <ownership>: when <ownership> is null it is a public supply open to all players; when <ownership> is a specific <player> it is a player supply accessible only to that player. Typical examples: Splendor's gem supply, Catan's resource card supply, per-player resource pools dealt from a common supply in some games.

description.zh: 从 <zone> 继承，此处说明：null 表示公共供应堆，所有玩家均可取用；指向特定 <player> 表示玩家供应堆，仅该玩家可取用。
description.en: Inherited from <zone>, clarified here: null means a public supply open to all players; a specific <player> means a player supply accessible only to that player.

definition.zh: 存放可见的、各不相同的 <object>，供 <player> 主动选择获取的 <reserve>。<market> 继承自 <reserve>。与 <supply> 的对偶概念——<supply> 存放无差别物件（<player> 只管「取多少」），<market> 存放各不相同物件（<player> 需要决定「取哪个」）。核心特征：(1) 物件各不相同——通常为 <piece>（如 <card>、<tile>），每件有独立的身份和 <property>；(2) 完全可见——所有物件面朝上陈列，成为所有 <player> 的公共信息；(3) 主动选择——<player> 从陈列的物件中指定具体哪一件来获取，而非无差别取用；(4) 获取通常伴随 <cost>——玩家支付对应费用后获得所选物件。典型例子：璀璨宝石的中央卡牌陈列区、四季物语的公共骰子区、 dominion 的王国卡牌供应区。
definition.en: A <reserve> that holds visible, distinct <object>s from which <player>s can actively choose and acquire. <market> extends <reserve>. The counterpart to <supply> — while <supply> holds undifferentiated items (player only decides 'how many'), <market> holds distinct items (player must decide 'which one'). Core traits: (1) items are distinct — typically <piece>s (e.g., <card>, <tile>), each with its own identity and <property>; (2) fully visible — all items are displayed face-up as public information for all <player>s; (3) active choice — <player>s designate a specific item to acquire rather than taking undifferentiated units; (4) acquisition usually involves a <cost> — the player pays the associated cost to obtain the chosen item. Typical examples: Splendor's central card display, Seasons' public dice pool, Dominion's Kingdom card supply.

description.zh: 市场展示 <object> 的数量上限。null 表示无固定上限。
description.en: Maximum number of <object>s this market can display. null means no fixed limit.

definition.zh: 存放有序叠放的 <object> 序列、从固定位置（通常为顶部）抽取的 <reserve>。<deck> 继承自 <reserve>。与 <supply> 和 <market> 不同——<supply> 无序取用、<market> 主动挑选，<deck> 则是从固定的抽取位置按序获取，玩家无法选择取哪一张。核心特征：(1) 有序序列——<object> 之间有严格的先后顺序；(2) 固定抽取位——每次从同一位置（顶部）取走最上方的一张；(3) 支持洗混——<shuffle> 可随机重排整个 <deck> 的顺序，是 <deck> 特有的操作；(4) 默认隐藏——面朝下放置，<information_visibility> 通常为 hidden，洗混后信息状态重置为不可预测。典型例子：Uno 的抽牌堆、璀璨宝石的贵族卡牌堆、卡坦岛的发展卡牌堆。
definition.en: A <reserve> that holds an ordered stack of <object>s, drawn from a fixed position (typically the top). <deck> extends <reserve>. Unlike <supply> (undifferentiated taking) and <market> (active choice), a <deck> is drawn from sequentially at a fixed position — the player cannot choose which one to take. Core traits: (1) ordered sequence — <object>s have a strict sequential order; (2) fixed draw position — the topmost <object> is always taken; (3) supports <shuffle> — randomly reordering is a <deck>-specific operation; (4) hidden by default — face-down, <information_visibility> is typically hidden, reset to unpredictable after <shuffle>. Typical examples: Uno's draw pile, Splendor's noble tile deck, Catan's development card deck.

definition.zh: 存放各不相同的 <object>、通过随机方式抽取的无序 <reserve>。<pool> 继承自 <reserve>。与 <deck> 的关键区别：<deck> 有固定顺序、从顶部按序抽取、支持 <shuffle>；<pool> 无序、每次抽取为独立随机事件、不支持 <shuffle>——你把手伸进袋子里摸一个，摸到什么是独立概率，不依赖之前的抽取。核心特征：(1) 无序集合——<object> 之间没有先后关系；(2) 随机抽取——每次获取哪一个由随机决定，非玩家选择（区别于 <market>），也非按序获取（区别于 <deck>）；(3) 身份后验——<object> 被抽出后其身份才公开；(4) 概率可调——向 <pool> 中添加或移除特定 <object> 可改变后续抽取的概率分布。典型例子：Scrabble 的字母袋、卡卡颂的板块抽袋、Orléans 的随从抽袋。
definition.en: An unordered <reserve> holding distinct <object>s, accessed by random draw. <pool> extends <reserve>. Key difference from <deck>: a <deck> has a fixed order, draws from the top sequentially, and supports <shuffle>; a <pool> is unordered, each draw is an independent random event, and <shuffle> is not supported — you reach into a bag and pull one out; what you get is an independent probability, not dependent on previous draws. Core traits: (1) unordered collection — no sequence among <object>s; (2) random draw — which one you get is determined randomly, not by player choice (unlike <market>) nor by sequence (unlike <deck>); (3) identity post-hoc — the <object>'s identity is only revealed after drawing; (4) adjustable probability — adding or removing specific <object>s changes the probability distribution of subsequent draws. Typical examples: Scrabble's letter bag, Carcassonne's tile bag, Orléans' follower bag.

definition.zh: 存放当前未进入游戏流程的 <object> 的 <reserve>。<game_box> 继承自 <reserve>。与 <supply>、<market>、<deck>、<pool> 不同——这些游戏中的 <reserve> 内容直接参与当前游戏状态和规则判定；而 <game_box> 中的 <object> 暂时游离于当前游戏流程之外，既不可被 <player> 取用，也不触发任何游戏规则。核心特征：(1) 初始容器——游戏设置前，所有组件通常先放在 <game_box> 中；(2) setup 阶段入口——游戏设置时从这里取出组件，放入合适的游戏内 <reserve>；(3) 流程外暂存——游戏过程中，某些规则可能要求将 <object> 移回 <game_box>，表示该 <object> 暂时从当前游戏流程中移除（区别于 <discard_pile> 的永久弃置）；(4) 不直接参与规则——<game_box> 中的 <object> 不计入胜负、不可被选择或操作，直到再次进入某个游戏内 <reserve>。典型例子：璀璨宝石盒中尚未分发的发展卡和贵族板块、某些游戏中被规则临时移出流程的卡牌或指示物。
definition.en: A <reserve> holding <object>s that are not currently part of the game flow. <game_box> extends <reserve>. Unlike <supply>, <market>, <deck>, and <pool> — in-game <reserve>s whose contents directly participate in the current game state and rules — <object>s in <game_box> are temporarily outside the current game flow: they cannot be taken by <player>s and trigger no game rules. Core traits: (1) initial container — before setup, all components usually start here; (2) setup entry point — during setup, components are taken from here and placed into appropriate in-game <reserve>s; (3) out-of-flow holding — during gameplay, certain rules may move <object>s back into <game_box>, indicating they are temporarily removed from the current game flow (distinct from permanent discarding to <discard_pile>); (4) non-participatory — <object>s in <game_box> do not count toward victory, cannot be selected or operated, until they re-enter an in-game <reserve>. Typical examples: undistributed development cards and noble tiles in the Splendor box, or cards/tokens temporarily removed from play by certain game rules.

definition.zh: 归属于单个 <player> 的私有 <player_zone>，用于存放该 <player> 已获得但尚未激活的 <piece> 或 <token>。<player_holding> 继承自 <player_zone>。其核心语义是「保留但未投入使用」——此区域中的 <object> 已经归该玩家所有，但尚未触发 <effect>，不直接参与公共游戏逻辑（如计分、战斗、生产）。<player> 通常可从 <player_holding> 中打出 <piece> 以将其移入公开区域。常见用途：手牌、已保留的卡牌、秘密任务指示物、未建造的板块、个人目标标记、仓库中的资源/材料。注意：因为其中的物件已经属于玩家，所以它不同于 <supply>（供应堆中的物件——无论 <ownership> 是公共还是玩家专属——通常尚未属于玩家）。
definition.en: A private <player_zone> belonging to a single <player>, holding <piece>s or <token>s that the <player> has acquired but not yet activated. <player_holding> extends <player_zone>. Its core semantic is 'reserved but not yet in play' — <object>s here already belong to the player but have not had their <effect>s triggered and do not directly participate in public game logic (e.g., scoring, combat, production). The <player> can typically <play> <piece>s from their <player_holding> to move them into a public zone. Common uses: hand cards, reserved cards, secret mission tokens, unbuilt tiles, personal objective markers, resources/materials in storage. Note: because its contents are already owned by the player, it is distinct from <supply> (whose contents — whether public or player-exclusive — are typically not yet owned).

definition.zh: 归属于单个 <player> 的公开 <player_zone>，用于放置该 <player> 已打出、已购买或已建造的 <piece>。<development_area> 继承自 <player_zone>。与 <player_holding> 构成对偶——<player_holding> 是「手里攥着还没用的」，<development_area> 是「已经摆出来正在生效的」。核心特征：(1) 公开可见——<information_visibility> 通常为 public，成为所有 <player> 判断对手实力的主要依据；(2) 效果激活——此区域中的 <piece> 的 <effect> 已经或正在持续生效，直接参与公共游戏逻辑；(3) 通常不可逆——<piece> 一旦进入此区域，通常无法退回 <player_holding>，除非规则明确允许。典型例子：万智牌中的战场、璀璨宝石中已购买的卡牌列、卡卡颂中已放置的地图板块。
definition.en: A public <player_zone> belonging to a single <player>, holding <piece>s that the <player> has played, purchased, or built. <development_area> extends <player_zone>. The counterpart to <player_holding> — <player_holding> is 'what you're holding but haven't used yet', <development_area> is 'what you've already deployed and is now taking effect'. Core traits: (1) publicly visible — <information_visibility> is typically public, making this the main basis for opponents to assess your strength; (2) effects active — <piece>s here have their <effect>s already or continuously active, directly participating in public game logic; (3) typically irreversible — once a <piece> enters this zone, it usually cannot be returned to <player_holding> unless explicitly allowed by rules. Typical examples: the battlefield in Magic: The Gathering, the purchased card row in Splendor, placed map tiles in Carcassonne.

definition.zh: 所有玩家共用的 <board>，承载公共游戏状态。<public_board> 继承自 <board>。它上面可以容纳公共 <zone>（如轨、展示区）、放置公共 <piece> 和 <token>，并可能携带自身的 <content>。<zone> 的存在和属性由游戏规则独立定义，<public_board> 是它们的物理宿主。物理形态不固定，可由多块板拼接而成；拼接而成的公共版图通过 <components> 列出其组成部分。
definition.en: A <board> shared by all players, carrying public game state. <public_board> extends <board>. It can host public <zone>s (e.g., tracks, display areas), hold public <piece>s and <token>s, and may carry its own <content>. <zone>s exist and are defined independently by game rules; the <public_board> is their physical host. Physical form is not fixed and may consist of multiple assembled boards; an assembled public board lists its parts via <components>.

description.zh: 当此公共版图由多块板拼接而成时，列出组成它的 <board> 或 <aid> 实例。单块公共版图可省略此字段。注意：此处只应包含 board 和纯参考 aid，不包含 <piece>、<tile> 等游戏零件——后者属于游戏状态，应放在 <zone> 中。
description.en: When this public board is physically assembled from multiple boards, list the <board> or <aid> instances that compose it. Omit for a single-piece board. Note: only boards and pure reference aids should be listed here; <piece>s, <tile>s, and other game components belong to game state and should reside in <zone>s.

description.zh: 组成公共版图的 <aid> 列表。用于表达「由多块 aid 拼成的公共版图」这一物理形态。
description.en: List of <aid>s composing the public board. Used to express a public board physically assembled from multiple aid parts.

definition.zh: 分配给单个 <player> 的专属 <board>，承载该玩家的个人游戏状态。<player_board> 继承自 <board>。它上面可以容纳该玩家专属的 <player_zone>（如模组区、仓库区、收入区等），并可能携带自身的 <content>（如面板上印着的基础活动图标）。通常每个 <player> 各持一块。与 <public_board> 的区别：<public_board> 全员共用，<player_board> 每人一块。
definition.en: A personal <board> assigned to a single <player>, carrying that player's individual game state. <player_board> extends <board>. It can host that player's personal <player_zone>s (e.g., module area, storage area, income area) and may carry its own <content> (e.g., the basic activity icon printed on it). Typically each <player> has one. Difference from <public_board>: <public_board> is shared by all, while <player_board> is one per player.

definition.zh: 记录规则摘要、流程参考或计分信息的便携 <aid>。<player_aid> 继承自 <aid>。通常为卡片或薄板形式，内容为游戏规则的浓缩或索引——如回合流程速查、所有 <action> 的图标说明、计分规则摘要。可有正反两面。
definition.en: A portable <aid> recording rule summaries, procedure references, or scoring information. <player_aid> extends <aid>. Typically a card or thin board containing condensed or indexed game rules — e.g., turn flow quick-reference, icon guide for all <action>s, scoring rule summary. May have two sides.

definition.zh: 完整记录游戏规则、流程和组件说明的文档型 <aid>。<rulebook> 继承自 <aid>。通常在游戏开始前阅读学习，游戏中可作为参考查阅。不参与游戏逻辑的运作——即使没有 <rulebook>，游戏规则依然存在并生效。<rulebook> 只是规则的书面载体，不是规则本身。
definition.en: A document-type <aid> that fully records the game's rules, procedures, and component descriptions. <rulebook> extends <aid>. Typically read before the game starts and used as a reference during play. Does not participate in game logic — even without the <rulebook>, the game rules still exist and apply. The <rulebook> is merely the written carrier of rules, not the rules themselves.

definition.zh: 游戏的虚构世界观、时代背景与关键角色设定，用于解释风味名称、主题和叙事元素，不直接参与规则判定。<setting> 继承自 <object>。例如，在《文明演化》中，玩家是创世技术学院的学生，正在参加名为「文明演化」的考试；考试场地是一片僻静的大陆，每位考生都必须成为当地的一名神祇，发展并引领自己的文明，在与其他文明的竞争中取得成功，胜者将晋升为创世技术学院的正式成员。阿格拉（Agera）是这场考试的主考官，因此代表考生获得其青睐程度的轨被称为 <favor_of_ager_track>（阿格拉恩惠轨）。
definition.en: The fictional world view, historical backdrop, and key character setup of a game, used to explain flavor names, themes, and narrative elements without directly participating in rule adjudication. <setting> extends <object>. For example, in Civolution, players are students of the Genesis Tech Academy taking an exam called 'Civilization Evolution'. The exam takes place on a remote continent; each candidate must become a local deity, develop and lead their own civilization, and outcompete the others. The winner becomes a full member of the Genesis Tech Academy. Agera is the examiner of this exam, so the track that records how much favor each candidate has earned is called the <favor_of_ager_track> (Favor of Agera track).

definition.zh: 一种有序的 <zone>，用于放置 <marker> 并记录某个数值或进度的当前状态。<track> 继承自 <zone>。与普通 zone 的区别在于：object 在 track 中通常只做内部位置移动（前进/后退），不发生 zone 之间的 transfer。典型例子包括计分轨、进程轨、天气轨、阶段序列、恩惠轨等。
definition.en: An ordered <zone> used to place <marker>s and record the current value or progress of some numeric or ordinal state. <track> extends <zone>. Unlike a regular zone, objects in a track usually only move internally (forward/backward) rather than being transferred between zones. Typical examples include score tracks, progress tracks, weather gauges, phase sequences, and favor tracks.

description.zh: 此轨存放的标记物类型。通常每个玩家在此放置一个 marker。
description.en: The type of markers this track holds. Usually each player places one marker on it.

description.zh: 此轨的刻度范围或单位描述。如「0–100 的环形计分轨」「0–12 的进程轨」。仅供展示和规则解释参考，不影响规则逻辑。
description.en: Description of the track's scale or range, e.g. '0–100 circular score track', '0–12 progress track'. For display and rule explanation only; does not affect rule logic.

description.zh: 轨的刻度范围或单位描述，用于规则讲解和 UI 展示。
description.en: Scale or range description of the track, used for rule explanation and UI display.

definition.zh: 用于记录 <player> 的 <score> 数量的 <track>。<score_track> 继承自 <track>。通常是公共版图的一部分或外框，每位玩家各用一个 <marker> 在此轨上指示自己当前拥有多少 <score>。<score> 本身是 <resource>，「玩家有 N 分」才是 <state>；分轨是这个 <state> 的可视化载体。
definition.en: A <track> used to record how much <score> each <player> has. <score_track> extends <track>. It is usually part of or the outer frame of the public board; each <player> uses a <marker> on this track to indicate how many <score> they currently have. <score> itself is a <resource>; 'Player has N points' is the <state>. The score track is the visual carrier of this <state>.

description.zh: 此轨存放所有玩家的分数标记。
description.en: This track holds all players' score markers.

definition.zh: 存放 <card> 的 <player_holding>，是最常见的玩家保留区形态。<hand> 继承自 <player_holding>。<information_visibility> 通常为 private（仅拥有者可观察）或 protected（拥有者可选择向其他 <player> 展示），但具体可见性由游戏规则决定。<hand> 是 <play> 的主要源区域——<player> 从手牌中打出 <card>，将其移入 <development_area> 或 <discard_pile>。
definition.en: A <player_holding> that holds <card>s, the most common form of player holding. <hand> extends <player_holding>. <information_visibility> is typically private (only the owner can observe) or protected (owner may choose to reveal to other <player>s), but the specific visibility is determined by game rules. <hand> is the primary source zone for <play> — a <player> plays a <card> from their hand, moving it to the <development_area> or <discard_pile>.

definition.zh: 使某个 <effect> 从静默（dormant）进入待结算（pending）状态的 <action>。<activation> 继承自 <action>。它是 <player> 对游戏规则说「我要使用这个效果」的声明——<player> 选择一张 <piece> 上的一个 <effect> 并将其激活，该 <effect> 随即进入 pending 状态，等待后续的 <resolve> 将其 <content> 应用到游戏 <state>。<activation> 不等同于 <resolve>——激活后效果可能排队等待，多个同时激活的 <effect> 需要通过优先级决定结算顺序。
definition.en: An <action> that transitions an <effect> from dormant to pending state. <activation> extends <action>. It is the <player>'s declaration to the game rules: 'I want to use this effect' — the <player> selects an <effect> on a <piece> and activates it, placing it in pending state to await subsequent <resolve> which applies its <content> to the game <state>. <activation> is not the same as <resolve> — after activation, effects may queue; multiple simultaneously activated <effect>s require priority ordering for resolution.

description.zh: 被激活的 <effect>。<activation> 的本质是使一个 <effect> 从静默转入待结算——没有 <effect>，激活无事可做。此约束要求子类指明激活的是哪个 <effect>。
description.en: The <effect> being activated. The essence of <activation> is transitioning an <effect> from dormant to pending — without an <effect>, activation has nothing to do. This constraint requires subclasses to specify which <effect> is being activated.

definition.zh: 用于产生随机数值的游戏组件。<dice> 继承自 <object>。每颗骰子有若干面，每面印有一个数值或符号；通过 <die_roll> 事件掷出后，根据朝上的一面确定结果。骰子本身没有 <effect>，不可被 <play>，只是随机数生成器。
definition.en: A game component used to generate random values. <dice> extends <object>. Each die has several faces, each printed with a value or symbol; after being rolled via a <die_roll> event, the result is determined by the face that lands upward. Dice themselves have no <effect> and cannot be <play>ed — they are random number generators.

description.zh: 骰子的面数。如六面骰为 6。
description.en: Number of faces on the die. E.g., 6 for a six-sided die.

description.zh: 骰子面数，用于规则说明和随机结果范围。
description.en: Number of faces, used for rule explanation and random result range.

definition.zh: 描述游戏版图上某片区域的自然或地貌类型。<terrain> 继承自 <object>。它是分类概念，本身不携带 <effect>，但会影响相邻、资源产出、移动等规则。典型例子包括森林、草原、山脉、水域等。
definition.en: A classification describing the natural or landscape type of an area on the game board. <terrain> extends <object>. It is a categorical concept that carries no <effect> itself but influences adjacency, resource production, movement, and other rules. Typical examples include Forest, Grassland, Mountains, Water, etc.

definition.zh: 由连续同类型 <terrain> 组成的一片版图区域。<region> 继承自 <zone>，是一种逻辑容器。同一 <terrain> 类型但不相连的部分算作不同 <region>；相邻 <region> 之间通过边界接壤。<region> 可以包含 <campsite>、<piece>、<token> 等，并可能关联一个 <terrain> 类型和一个 <material_tile>。
definition.en: A board area consisting of contiguous spaces of the same <terrain> type. <region> extends <zone> as a logical container. Areas of the same <terrain> type that are not connected count as separate <region>s; adjacent <region>s share a border. A <region> may contain <campsite>s, <piece>s, <token>s, and may be associated with a <terrain> type and a material tile.

description.zh: 此区域的地形类型。
description.en: The terrain type of this region.

description.zh: 区域所属的地形类型。
description.en: The terrain type this region belongs to.

definition.zh: 位于 <region> 内的特定位置，用于容纳 <tribe> 等 <piece>。<campsite> 继承自 <object>。一个 <region> 内可能有多个 <campsite>，某些营地可能有特殊效果（如火边营地提供分数）。<campsite> 本身不改变游戏状态，只是位置标记。
definition.en: A specific location within a <region> that can hold <piece>s such as <tribe>s. <campsite> extends <object>. A <region> may contain multiple <campsite>s, and some campsites may have special effects (e.g., fire encampments grant points). A <campsite> itself does not change game state; it is merely a position marker.

definition.zh: 放置在公共版图上、影响相邻 <region> 的特殊 <tile>。<site> 继承自 <tile>。通常初始背面朝上，通过特定 <action>（如探索）翻开后生效。每个 <site> 有独特的被动效果，在特定阶段或触发条件下结算。
definition.en: A special <tile> placed on the public board that affects adjacent <region>s. <site> extends <tile>. Usually placed face down at the start and revealed by a specific <action> (e.g., exploration) to take effect. Each <site> has a unique passive effect that resolves in specific phases or under trigger conditions.

definition.zh: 满足其中任意一个即可的费用形式。<alternative_cost> 继承自 <property>。用于表达「支付 A 或满足 B 即可」的规则——玩家只需完成所列条件之一，该费用即视为已支付。多个替代条件之间是 OR 关系。
definition.en: A cost form where fulfilling any one of the listed conditions is sufficient. <alternative_cost> extends <property>. Used to express rules like 'pay A or satisfy B' — the player only needs to complete one of the listed conditions for the cost to be considered paid. Multiple alternative conditions are in an OR relationship.

description.zh: 可供选择的替代条件列表。玩家只需满足其中一项。
description.en: List of alternative conditions; the player only needs to satisfy one.

description.zh: 替代条件选项列表，玩家满足其中任意一个即可。
description.en: List of alternative cost options; satisfying any one is enough.

definition.zh: 描述玩家在执行某个 <action> 或 <effect> 时必须做出的多选一决策。<choice> 继承自 <property>。它本身不是费用或效果，而是对「玩家必须选择一项」这一规则事实的声明。典型例子：「二选一行动」「从三种资源中选择一种」。
definition.en: Describes a multi-option decision a player must make when executing an <action> or <effect>. <choice> extends <property>. It is neither a cost nor an effect itself, but a declaration of the rule fact that 'the player must choose one option'. Typical examples: 'choose one of two actions', 'choose one of three resources'.

description.zh: 可选的选项列表。每个选项是一个规格对象，由具体游戏规则定义。
description.en: List of available options. Each option is a specification object defined by the game rules.

description.zh: 玩家可选择的选项列表。
description.en: List of options available to the player.

definition.zh: 持续生效、无需玩家主动触发的效果规格。<passive_effect> 继承自 <property>。与需要 <activation> 的 <effect> 不同，被动效果一旦满足其前提条件就会自动生效，常见于 <site>、已安装的 <card> 或 <attribute_chip>。其运行时不产生独立的 <event>，而是修改规则判定或提供额外奖励。
definition.en: A continuously active effect specification that does not require the player to actively trigger it. <passive_effect> extends <property>. Unlike <effect>s that require <activation>, passive effects automatically apply once their prerequisites are met, commonly found on <site>s, installed <card>s, or <attribute_chip>s. At runtime they do not produce standalone <event>s but modify rule evaluations or grant additional bonuses.

description.zh: 此被动效果的生效前提。null 表示始终生效。
description.en: The prerequisite for this passive effect to apply. null means always active.

description.zh: 被动效果的生效前提，null 表示无条件持续生效。
description.en: Prerequisite for the passive effect; null means always active.

definition.zh: 投掷一颗或多颗 <dice> 以产生随机数值的 <event>。<die_roll> 继承自 <event>。结果由骰子朝上的一面决定，可用于判定、费用、资源获取等。玩家通常可以花费创意标记等资源修改骰子点数。
definition.en: An <event> in which one or more <dice> are rolled to generate random values. <die_roll> extends <event>. The result is determined by the face(s) that land upward and can be used for checks, costs, resource gains, etc. Players may often spend resources such as idea markers to modify die results.

definition.zh: 投掷玩家持有的全部粉骰子，并根据 <favor_of_ager_track> 当前位置判定是否通过的 <event>。<favor_test> 继承自 <event>。只要有一颗骰子的点数落在轨道允许的范围内，即视为通过。常用于模组升级后的额外行动。
definition.en: An <event> in which a player rolls all their fate dice and checks whether any die result falls within the range allowed by the current position on the Favor of Agera track. <favor_test> extends <event>. Passing requires at least one die to show an allowed value. Commonly used for bonus actions after upgrading modules.

definition.zh: 改变一个 <effect> 的 level state 的 <event>。<upgrade> 继承自 <event>。升级的本质是 state change——effect 的 level 从 N 变为 N+1，对应的 cost 和 content 随之变化。常见的物理表现（翻面、移除上层板块露出下层）是 state change 的后果，而非升级的原因——规则要求玩家「作为升级的结果，将板块翻面」，而非「因为翻了面，所以升级了」。因果关系：state change 在先，物理操作是规则指令的被执行结果。
definition.en: An <event> that changes the level state of an <effect>. <upgrade> extends <event>. The essence of an upgrade is a state change — the effect's level goes from N to N+1, and the corresponding cost and content change accordingly. Common physical manifestations (flipping, removing the upper tile to reveal the lower layer) are consequences of the state change, not its cause — the rules instruct the player 'as a result of upgrading, flip the tile', not 'because you flipped it, it is now upgraded'. Causality: state change comes first; the physical operation is the executed result of the rules' instruction.

definition.zh: 将一个 <piece>（通常为 <card>）从其当前 <zone>（如 <player_holding>、<market>）转移至公开 <zone>（通常为 <development_area> 或 <discard_pile>）并使其生效的 <event>。<play> 继承自 <event>。它是桌游中最核心的入场操作——一张 <piece> 脱离原有区域、进入公开/已使用状态，其 <effect> 自此生效。<play> 不一定由 <player> 主动发起：它可以是玩家 <action> 的直接内容（玩家主动打出一张牌），也可以是 <trigger> 的 <event> 列表中的一员（如「购买」规则中，支付 <cost> 后由规则自动将卡牌打出入场）——并非所有打出都是玩家主动想做的。<play> 在物理层面必然包含物件位移，但在逻辑层面独立于 <transfer>——<play> 侧重入场合法性（<cost> 是否已支付、时机是否正确）及后续 <effect> 的生效，而非单纯的位移。
definition.en: An <event> that moves a <piece> (typically a <card>) from its current <zone> (e.g., a <player_holding>, a <market>) to a public <zone> (typically a <development_area> or <discard_pile>) and puts it into effect. <play> extends <event>. It is the most central enter-play operation in board games — a <piece> leaves its original zone, enters a public/used state, and its <effect> takes effect from then on. <play> is not necessarily initiated by a <player>: it can be the direct content of a player <action> (a player actively playing a card), or a member of a <trigger>'s <event> list (e.g., in a 'purchase' rule, after the <cost> is paid, the rules automatically play the card into play) — not every play is something a player actively chooses to do. <play> necessarily involves physical displacement, but is logically distinct from <transfer> — <play> focuses on enter-play legality (has the <cost> been paid, is the timing correct) and subsequent <effect>s taking effect, rather than mere displacement.

description.zh: 被打出的 <piece>。<play> 的本质是玩家选择一张 <piece> 并将其投入使用——没有 <piece>，打出操作无事可做。此约束要求子类指明打出的是哪张 <piece>。
description.en: The <piece> being played. The essence of <play> is a player selecting a <piece> and putting it into use — without a <piece>, play has nothing to do. This constraint requires subclasses to specify which <piece> is being played.
